question_english: What is the primary objective of ensuring "transparency" in public procurement according to the General Financial Rules (GFR), 2017?
options_english: To ensure that procurement processes, criteria, and decisions are clear, open, fair, and systematically documented.
To publish the personal bank account numbers and confidential financial assets of all participating commercial vendors.
To mandate that all public goods and services are sourced exclusively through accredited multinational foreign suppliers.
To provide unrestricted public access to trade secrets, proprietary technology, and confidential commercial data of competing bidders.
explanation_english: Under Rule 144(vii) and Rule 173 of the General Financial Rules (GFR), 2017, transparency is one of the foundational pillars of public procurement along with economy, efficiency, fairness, and accountability. Ensuring transparency means that all stages of the procurement lifecycle—including tender notification, technical specifications, qualification criteria, bid evaluation methodology, and contract award decisions—are well-defined, published openly to all eligible participants, and systematically documented on official records. For a school Principal or Drawing and Disbursing Officer (DDO), maintaining complete transparency eliminates administrative arbitrariness, prevents corruption and favouritism, fosters healthy market competition, and creates an auditable record essential for statutory audits by CAG and departmental inspections. Transparency does not require revealing proprietary trade secrets of bidders or personal bank account data, which remain protected under commercial confidentiality.
explanation_hindi: सामान्य वित्तीय नियम (GFR), 2017 के नियम 144(vii) तथा नियम 173 के अंतर्गत सार्वजनिक खरीद में पारदर्शिता (Transparency) एक मूलभूत सिद्धांत है। इसका मुख्य उद्देश्य यह सुनिश्चित करना है कि निविदा आमंत्रण, तकनीकी विनिर्देश, योग्यता शर्तें, मूल्यांकन मानदंड और अनुबंध प्रदान करने के निर्णय पूरी तरह स्पष्ट, खुले, पूर्वाग्रह-मुक्त और आधिकारिक रूप से प्रलेखित (documented) हों। विद्यालय के प्राचार्य अथवा आहरण एवं संवितरण अधिकारी (DDO) के रूप में पारदर्शी व्यवस्था अपनाने से प्रशासनिक मनमानेपन और भ्रष्टाचार पर रोक लगती है, पात्र विक्रेताओं को समान अवसर मिलता है, तथा वित्तीय लेखापरीक्षा (CAG Audit) के लिए एक स्पष्ट साक्ष्य उपलब्ध रहता है। पारदर्शिता का आशय किसी भी प्रकार से बोलीदाताओं के गोपनीय व्यापारिक रहस्यों या व्यक्तिगत वित्तीय ब्योरे को उजागर करना नहीं होता।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) To ensure procurement processes and decisions are clear, open, and documented.

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: decisions are clear, open, and documented. Transparency in public buying ensures that all stages of the procurement process--including tender notification, evaluation criteria, bidding procedures, and award decisions--are clearly defined, open to qualified participants, and systematically documented. Clear, publicly accessible procedures build commercial confidence, prevent corrupt practices, ensure equal opportunity for prospective bidders, and enable effective administrative oversight and post-procurement auditing.

question_hindi: GFR 2017 के अंतर्गत सार्वजनिक खरीद के मूलभूत सिद्धांतों के संबंध में निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा युग्म गलत है?

question_english: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECT regarding the fundamental principles of public procurement under GFR 2017?
options_english: Economy - Procuring required goods and services of requisite quality at the most competitive and reasonable market price
Efficiency - Ensuring timely completion of procurement workflows while strictly avoiding procedural and administrative delays
Equality - Reserving all government supply contracts exclusively for large multinational corporations
Transparency - Maintaining an open, competitive, and publicly accessible bidding process with clear specifications
explanation_english: Rule 144 of GFR 2017 establishes the fundamental principles of public buying: Economy, Efficiency, Effectiveness, Equity (Equality/Fairness), and Transparency. The principle of 'Equality' (or Fair Treatment) dictates that every eligible vendor must receive equal opportunity and unbiased treatment without arbitrary discrimination or preferential bias. Restricting procurement contracts solely to large multinational corporations is a flagrant violation of this principle. Furthermore, government procurement frameworks such as the Public Procurement Policy for Micro and Small Enterprises (MSEs) Order, 2012 and the 'Make in India' (Preference to Make in India) Order actively mandate reservation and purchase preferences for domestic MSMEs and local suppliers to promote inclusive industrial growth, completely contradicting the idea of exclusivity for multinational corporations.
explanation_hindi: GFR 2017 का नियम 144 सार्वजनिक खरीद के मूल सिद्धांतों (मितव्ययिता, दक्षता, प्रभावशीलता, निष्पक्षता/समानता और पारदर्शिता) को प्रतिपादित करता है। 'समानता और निष्पक्षता' (Equality and Fairness) के सिद्धांत का अर्थ है कि सभी पात्र आपूर्तिकर्ताओं और बोलीदाताओं को बिना किसी भेदभाव के समान अवसर प्राप्त हो। सरकारी अनुबंधों को केवल बड़ी बहुराष्ट्रीय कंपनियों के लिए आरक्षित करना इस सिद्धांत का प्रत्यक्ष उल्लंघन है। इसके विपरीत, सरकार की सूक्ष्म और लघु उद्यम (MSE) खरीद नीति तथा 'मेक इन इंडिया' नीति के तहत स्थानीय सूक्ष्म, लघु और मध्यम उद्यमों (MSMEs) को प्राथमिकता एवं आरक्षण दिया जाता है, न कि बहुराष्ट्रीय कंपनियों का एकाधिकार स्थापित किया जाता है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (C) Equality - Reserving all contracts only for large multinational corporations

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: large multinational corporations The principle of equality in public procurement requires granting equal opportunity and fair access to all eligible suppliers without administrative bias or arbitrary discrimination. Restricting government contracts exclusively to large multinational corporations violates equality principles. Public buying rules actively encourage participation from diverse market participants, including micro, small, and medium enterprises, ensuring broad-based and fair commercial competition.

question_hindi: GFR 2017 के तहत सरकारी खरीद के संदर्भ में "बोली दस्तावेज़" (Bid Document / निविदा दस्तावेज़) का क्या तात्पर्य है?
options_hindi: बजट आवंटन और धनराशि की स्वीकृति हेतु प्रशासनिक प्रमुख द्वारा वित्त विभाग को प्रस्तुत किया गया औपचारिक प्रस्ताव।

संस्थागत भंडार कक्ष में भंडारपाल द्वारा संधारित स्थायी स्टॉक रजिस्टर जिसमें प्राप्त संपत्तियों की प्रविष्टि की जाती है।

question_english: In the context of government procurement under GFR 2017, what does the term "Bid Document" (or Tender Document) signify?
options_english: The formal proposal submitted by an administrative head to the finance ministry for budget sanction and fund release.
The commercial invoice and delivery receipt presented by the vendor to the treasury officer for final settlement.
The permanent dead stock register maintained in the institutional storeroom recording received assets.
The comprehensive official document issued by the buyer containing instructions, technical specifications, terms, and evaluation criteria.
explanation_english: Under Rule 168 of GFR 2017 and the Manual for Procurement of Goods, a 'Bid Document' (or Tender Document / Request for Proposal) is the official dossier prepared and issued by the procuring entity to invite bids from prospective suppliers. It lays down all technical requirements, functional specifications, delivery schedules, terms and conditions of contract (both General Conditions of Contract - GCC, and Special Conditions of Contract - SCC), instructions to bidders (ITB), bid evaluation methodology, and qualification criteria. For an institutional head or DDO, the bid document serves as the legal and operational bedrock for evaluating competing bids objectively and concluding an enforceable public contract.
explanation_hindi: GFR 2017 के नियम 168 तथा माल खरीद नियमावली के अनुसार, 'बोली दस्तावेज़' (Bid Document / Tender Document) खरीद प्राधिकरण द्वारा जारी किया गया वह वैधानिक दस्तावेज़ है जिसके आधार पर पात्र बोलीदाताओं से निविदाएं आमंत्रित की जाती हैं। इस दस्तावेज़ में बोलीदाताओं के लिए निर्देश (ITB), विस्तृत तकनीकी विनिर्देश, गुणवत्ता मानक, संविदा की सामान्य और विशेष शर्तें (GCC व SCC), पात्रता शर्तें, मूल्यांकन पद्धति और आपूर्ति की समय-सीमा स्पष्ट रूप से वर्णित होती है। यह क्रेता और विक्रेता के बीच पारदर्शी, निष्पक्ष और निष्पादनीय अनुबंध का आधार बनता है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (D) The document issued containing instructions, specifications, contract conditions, and evaluation criteria.

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: instructions, specifications, contract conditions, and evaluation criteria. A bid document is a comprehensive official dossier issued by a procuring authority to invite commercial offers from potential suppliers. It sets out detailed technical specifications, operational scope, performance parameters, bidding instructions, general and special contract terms, evaluation criteria, and submission deadlines. It serves as the legal and technical baseline for evaluating incoming bids and establishing contract agreements.

question_hindi: GFR 2017 के प्रावधानों के अनुसार, निम्नलिखित में से किसे बोली दस्तावेज़ (Bid Document) में शामिल नहीं किया जाना चाहिए?
options_hindi: प्रस्तुत बोलियों को आधिकारिक रूप से खोलने की सटीक तिथि, समय तथा भौतिक या ऑनलाइन स्थान
आवश्यक वस्तुओं के विस्तृत तकनीकी विनिर्देश, कार्यात्मक मानक और गुणवत्ता के पैमाने
अस्पष्ट, अपरिभाषित या व्यक्तिपरक (subjective) मूल्यांकन मानदंड जो खरीद प्राधिकरण को मनमाना विवेकाधिकार प्रदान करते हों
भुगतान की व्यापक शर्तें, संवितरण अनुसूची और आवश्यक परफॉर्मेंस सिक्योरिटी (निष्पादन गारंटी) की मांग
source: AI-generated from supplied reference material; General Financial Rules (GFR), 2017

question_english: According to the provisions of GFR 2017, which of the following elements must NOT be incorporated into a Bid Document?
options_english: The exact date, time, and mode/venue for the official opening of submitted bids
Detailed technical specifications, functional parameters, and quality benchmarks of the goods required
Vague, undefined, or subjective evaluation criteria that confer discretionary powers upon the procuring authority
Comprehensive terms of payment, milestone disbursements, and required performance security guarantees
explanation_english: Rule 173 of GFR 2017 strictly prescribes that the evaluation criteria in a tender document must be clear, quantifiable, objective, and unambiguous to eliminate arbitrariness, favouritism, and subjective bias. Bid documents must state all criteria in precise terms so that bidders understand how their proposals will be judged. Including vague or subjective parameters confers unchecked discretion upon the evaluation committee, which is contrary to the core procurement principles of transparency and fairness. Essential elements that must be included are bid opening details, technical specifications, payment terms, and warranty/security requirements.
explanation_hindi: GFR 2017 के नियम 173 के तहत यह अनिवार्य है कि निविदा दस्तावेज़ में मूल्यांकन मानदंड स्पष्ट, निष्पक्ष, वस्तुनिष्ठ (objective) और मापने योग्य होने चाहिए ताकि किसी भी प्रकार के मनमानेपन या पक्षपात को समाप्त किया जा सके। बोली दस्तावेज़ में अस्पष्ट या व्यक्तिपरक (subjective) मानदंड शामिल करना पूरी तरह निषिद्ध है क्योंकि इससे खरीद समिति को अनुचित विवेकाधिकार मिलता है, जो खरीद की निष्पक्षता को भंग करता है। बोलियां खोलने का समय/स्थान, तकनीकी विनिर्देश, भुगतान शर्तें और निष्पादन गारंटी जैसे स्पष्ट नियम बोली दस्तावेज़ के अनिवार्य अंग हैं।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (C) Vague and subjective evaluation criteria that give arbitrary discretion to the buyer

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: that give arbitrary discretion to the buyer Bid documents must clearly state objective, unambiguous, and measurable evaluation parameters to ensure total fairness and transparency in vendor selection. Including vague or subjective evaluation criteria grants arbitrary discretion to the procuring official, which violates fundamental procurement principles. All criteria regarding technical eligibility, price evaluation, payment terms, delivery schedules, and required guarantees must be precisely defined.

question_hindi: GFR 2017 के नियम 154 के अनुसार, सक्षम प्राधिकारी द्वारा एक निर्धारित प्रमाण पत्र दर्ज करने की शर्त पर, बिना कोटेशन या बोलियां आमंत्रित किए किसी भी अवसर पर सीधे माल खरीद की अधिकतम वित्तीय सीमा क्या है?

question_english: Under Rule 154 of GFR 2017, what is the prescribed financial ceiling for the direct purchase of goods on each occasion without inviting quotations or bids, subject to recording a certificate by the competent authority?
explanation_english: Rule 154 of the General Financial Rules (GFR), 2017 provides for 'Purchase of goods without quotation'. Under this rule, purchase of goods up to the value of Rs. 25,000/- (Rupees Twenty-Five Thousand) only on each occasion may be made without inviting quotations or bids, on the basis of a certificate to be recorded by the competent authority in the prescribed format: 'I, am personally satisfied that these goods purchased are of the requisite quality and specification and have been purchased from a reliable supplier at a reasonable price.' For a school Principal acting as Head of Office / DDO, this enables swift procurement of urgent, petty institutional supplies without procedural delays, provided purchases are not intentionally split to circumvent higher procurement formalities (Rule 157).
explanation_hindi: सामान्य वित्तीय नियम (GFR), 2017 के नियम 154 में 'कोटेशन के बिना माल की खरीद' (Purchase of goods without quotation) का प्रावधान है। इसके अंतर्गत सक्षम प्राधिकारी द्वारा निर्धारित प्रारूप में एक प्रमाण पत्र दर्ज करके प्रत्येक अवसर पर ₹25,000/- (पच्चीस हजार रुपये) तक के मूल्य का माल बिना कोई निविदा या कोटेशन आमंत्रित किए सीधे खरीदा जा सकता है। प्रमाण पत्र में यह प्रमाणित करना अनिवार्य होता है: 'मैं व्यक्तिगत रूप से संतुष्ट हूँ कि खरीदी गई सामग्री अपेक्षित गुणवत्ता और विनिर्देश की है तथा एक विश्वसनीय आपूर्तिकर्ता से उचित बाजार मूल्य पर खरीदी गई है।' विद्यालय के प्राचार्य/DDO तात्कालिक आवश्यकताओं हेतु इस नियम का उपयोग कर सकते हैं, बशर्ते उच्च वित्तीय प्रक्रियाओं से बचने के लिए मांग को जानबूझकर टुकड़ों में न बांटा गया हो (नियम 157)।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (B) Rs. 25,000/-

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Rule 154 of the General Financial Rules 2017 permits the direct purchase of goods valued up to twenty-five thousand rupees on each occasion without inviting formal quotations or tenders. This relaxation applies provided the competent authority certifies in writing that the procured goods meet requisite quality standards, suit departmental requirements, and were purchased at a reasonable market price.

question_hindi: एक विद्यालय के प्राचार्य को कक्षाओं के लिए ₹1,50,000/- के ड्यूल डेस्क खरीदने हैं। यदि यह सामग्री गवर्नमेंट ई-मार्केटप्लेस (GeM) पर उपलब्ध नहीं है, तो GFR 2017 के अनुसार इस खरीद को करने की सर्वाधिक उपयुक्त विधि कौन-सी है?

question_english: A school Principal needs to purchase dual desks worth Rs. 1,50,000/- for classrooms. According to GFR 2017, what is the most appropriate procurement method if the required items are certified as not available on the Government e-Marketplace (GeM)?
options_english: Direct cash purchase from a single nearby vendor without seeking competitive quotations.
Publishing an Advertised Tender Enquiry across leading national newspapers and public portals.
Single Tender Enquiry awarded directly to an unverified local furniture supplier.
Procurement through a Local Purchase Committee comprising three members as approved by the competent authority.
explanation_english: Under Rule 155 of GFR 2017 ('Purchase of goods by Purchase Committee'), purchase of goods costing above Rs. 25,000/- and up to Rs. 2,50,000/- on each occasion may be carried out on the recommendations of a duly constituted Local Purchase Committee (LPC) consisting of three members appointed by the Head of Department/Competent Authority. When the goods are not available on GeM, the committee conducts an offline or local market survey to identify suitable suppliers, ascertains price reasonableness and quality, obtains quotations, and prepares a joint survey certificate before recommending the purchase. Since Rs. 1,50,000/- falls squarely between Rs. 25,000 and Rs. 2,50,000, procurement via a 3-member Local Purchase Committee is the exact prescribed procedure.
explanation_hindi: GFR 2017 के नियम 155 ('क्रय समिति द्वारा माल की खरीद') के अनुसार, प्रत्येक अवसर पर ₹25,000/- से अधिक और ₹2,50,000/- तक की लागत वाली वस्तुओं की खरीद विभागाध्यक्ष/सक्षम प्राधिकारी द्वारा गठित तीन सदस्यों की एक 'स्थानीय क्रय समिति' (LPC) की सिफारिश पर की जा सकती है। यदि वस्तुएं GeM पर उपलब्ध नहीं हैं, तो यह समिति बाजार सर्वेक्षण करती है, प्रतिष्ठित आपूर्तिकर्ताओं से दरों का पता लगाती है, गुणवत्ता और मूल्य की औचित्यता की जांच करती है तथा संयुक्त प्रमाण पत्र तैयार करके खरीद की सिफारिश करती है। चूँकि ₹1,50,000/- की राशि ₹25,000 से ₹2.5 लाख के मध्य आती है, अतः तीन सदस्यीय स्थानीय क्रय समिति के माध्यम से खरीद करना ही नियमानुकूल प्रक्रिया है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (D) Purchase through a Local Purchase Committee of three members as decided by Head of Department.

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Committee of three members as decided by Head of Department. For procuring goods valued above twenty-five thousand rupees and up to two lakh fifty thousand rupees on each occasion when not available on GeM, Rule 155 mandates purchase through a three-member Local Purchase Committee. The committee conducts a local market survey, evaluates suitable suppliers, certifies quality and price reasonableness, and jointly recommends the most appropriate purchase offer.

question_hindi: GFR 2017 के नियम 163 के अंतर्गत "टू-बिड सिस्टम" (तकनीकी और वित्तीय बोलियों की एक साथ प्राप्ति) का सही वर्णन निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा कथन करता है?
options_hindi: तकनीकी बोली और वित्तीय बोली दो अलग-अलग सीलबंद लिफाफों में एक साथ जमा की जाती हैं, और वित्तीय बोलियां केवल तकनीकी रूप से योग्य बोलीदाताओं की ही खोली जाती हैं।

एक ही बोलीदाता को एक ही दस्तावेज़ दो बार जमा करना अनिवार्य होता है—पहले भौतिक रूप से और फिर ऑनलाइन पोर्टल पर।

question_english: Which of the following statements correctly describes the "Two-Bid System" (simultaneous receipt of technical and financial bids) under Rule 163 of GFR 2017?
options_english: Technical bids and financial bids are submitted simultaneously in two separate sealed covers, with the financial bids opened only for technically qualified bidders.
Bids are invited exclusively from two pre-selected and pre-registered commercial vendors on a rotation basis.
A single bidder is required to submit the exact same bid document twice—first physically and subsequently via an online portal.
Two distinct government departments participate as competing buyers bidding against one another in an open market auction.
explanation_english: Rule 163 of GFR 2017 outlines the 'Two-Bid System' (simultaneous receipt of technical and financial bids). For purchasing high-value plant, machinery, specialized IT equipment, or complex goods, bids are invited in two separate sealed envelopes: one containing the 'Technical Bid' (commercial terms, technical compliance, certifications, client references) and the other containing the 'Financial Bid' (price schedule). Initially, only the technical bids are opened and evaluated against pre-disclosed criteria. The financial bids of only those bidders who are found technically responsive and qualified are opened on a notified date in the presence of bidders. Financial bids of disqualified bidders are returned unopened. This safeguards against lower-quality goods being selected merely due to artificially low pricing.
explanation_hindi: GFR 2017 के नियम 163 में 'द्वि-बोली प्रणाली' (Two-Bid System) का उल्लेख है। उच्च मूल्य की मशीनरी, वैज्ञानिक उपकरणों या जटिल तकनीकी वस्तुओं की खरीद हेतु बोलीदाताओं से दो अलग-अलग सीलबंद लिफाफों में एक साथ बोलियां मांगी जाती हैं—एक लिफाफे में 'तकनीकी बोली' (तकनीकी विनिर्देश, योग्यता प्रमाण पत्र, आदि) और दूसरे में 'वित्तीय बोली' (दरें/मूल्य)। प्रथम चरण में केवल तकनीकी बोलियां खोली और जांची जाती हैं। केवल उन्हीं बोलीदाताओं की वित्तीय बोलियां खोली जाती हैं जो तकनीकी मूल्यांकन में योग्य (technically qualified) पाए जाते हैं। अयोग्य बोलीदाताओं की वित्तीय बोलियां बिना खोले वापस कर दी जाती हैं, जिससे केवल कम कीमत के आधार पर घटिया गुणवत्ता वाली वस्तुओं के चयन का जोखिम समाप्त हो जाता है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) Technical and financial bids are submitted simultaneously in two separate sealed envelopes.

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: simultaneously in two separate sealed envelopes. Under Rule 163, the two-bid system requires bidders to submit their technical qualifications and commercial prices simultaneously in two separate, sealed envelopes. The procuring authority opens and evaluates the technical proposals first. Financial bids are subsequently opened only for those bidders whose technical offers fully meet the mandatory technical requirements, thereby preventing financial considerations from compromising technical quality standards.

question_english:
Consider the following statements regarding an Advertised Tender Enquiry (Open Tender) under Rule 161 of GFR 2017:
I. It should be adopted for the procurement of goods of estimated value of Rs. 25 lakhs and above.
II. The tender advertisement must mandatorily be published on the Central Public Procurement Portal (CPPP).
III. The minimum time allowed for the submission of domestic bids should ordinarily be three days from the date of publication.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
options_english: I and II only
II and III only
I and III only
I, II and III
explanation_english:
Under Rule 161 of GFR 2017:
1. Statement I is correct: Advertised Tender Enquiry (Open Competitive Bidding) is the standard method for procurement of goods of estimated value of Rs. 25 Lakhs and above.
2. Statement II is correct: Publication of tender notices on the Central Public Procurement Portal (CPPP) at www.eprocure.gov.in and on the ministry/department's website is mandatory. It is also published on GeM.
3. Statement III is incorrect: The minimum time allowed for submission of bids should ordinarily be three weeks (21 days) from the date of publication of the tender notice or availability of bidding documents for domestic tenders, and four weeks for international tenders. A window of only three days is completely inadequate and contrary to GFR rules.
Hence, only statements I and II are correct.

question_english:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).
Assertion (A): Limited Tender Enquiry can be adopted as a method of procurement for goods of estimated value up to Rs. 25 lakhs.
Reason (R): Under Limited Tender Enquiry, copies of the bidding document should be sent directly by speed post, registered post, courier, or email to at least three registered suppliers.
In light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options_english: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is true but (R) is false
(A) is false but (R) is true
explanation_english:
Under Rule 162 of GFR 2017:
1. Assertion (A) is true: Limited Tender Enquiry (LTE) is standardly adopted for procurement of goods where the estimated value is up to Rs. 25 Lakhs (Rule 162(i)). It strikes a balance between procurement efficiency and competition for moderate value purchases.
2. Reason (R) is true: Under Rule 162(ii), bidding documents in an LTE must be dispatched directly to all registered suppliers for the goods in question, and the number of supplier firms in LTE should normally be more than three (at least three registered suppliers).
3. Relationship: While both statements are legally accurate provisions of Rule 162, Reason (R) describes the communication and dispatch protocol to registered suppliers; it does not explain WHY the financial threshold was fixed at Rs. 25 lakhs (which was determined by the Government on grounds of administrative convenience and balancing transaction costs against competitive depth). Therefore, (R) is not the logical explanation of (A).

question_english:
Arrange the following sequential stages of a standard public procurement cycle under GFR 2017 in the correct chronological order:
I. Evaluation of technical and financial bids
II. Assessment of need and formulation of technical specifications
III. Award of contract and issuance of purchase order
IV. Publication of tender notice and invitation of bids
options_english: II, IV, I, III
IV, II, I, III
II, I, IV, III
IV, I, II, III
explanation_english:
A standard public procurement cycle under GFR 2017 and procurement manuals follows a strict chronological workflow:
1. Stage II (Need & Specifications): The procuring entity determines the precise institutional need, checks budget availability, and frames generic, objective technical specifications (Rule 144).
2. Stage IV (Tender Publication): The bid document is issued and published on the Central Public Procurement Portal (CPPP) or GeM to invite offers (Rule 161/162).
3. Stage I (Bid Evaluation): Submitted bids are opened publicly, evaluated by a designated tender committee on technical and financial grounds against the pre-disclosed criteria (Rule 163/173).
4. Stage III (Contract Award): The competent financial authority approves the recommendation of the lowest evaluated responsive bidder (L1) and issues the formal contract/purchase order (Rule 173(xxi)).
Therefore, the correct chronological order is II -> IV -> I -> III.
explanation_hindi:

1. चरण II (आवश्यकता और विनिर्देश निर्धारण): सर्वप्रथम संस्थागत आवश्यकता का निर्धारण, बजट की उपलब्धता की जांच और गैर-स्वामित्व वाले सामान्य तकनीकी विनिर्देश तैयार किए जाते हैं (नियम 144)।

3. चरण I (बोलियों का मूल्यांकन): प्राप्त बोलियों को सार्वजनिक रूप से खोला जाता है और निविदा समिति द्वारा पूर्व-निर्धारित मानदंडों पर तकनीकी एवं वित्तीय मूल्यांकन किया जाता है (नियम 163/173)।

अतः सही क्रम II -> IV -> I -> III है।

question_english: Under Rule 170 of GFR 2017, what is the standard percentage range of the estimated value of goods that must be demanded as Bid Security (Earnest Money Deposit - EMD) from participating bidders?
explanation_english: Rule 170 of GFR 2017 prescribes the provisions for 'Bid Security' (Earnest Money Deposit - EMD). To safeguard against frivolous or irresponsible bidders withdrawing or altering their bids during the bid validity period, procuring authorities obtain Bid Security from bidders. The amount of Bid Security should ordinarily range between two percent to five percent (2% to 5%) of the estimated value of the goods to be procured. The bid security may be accepted in the form of Account Payee Demand Draft, Fixed Deposit Receipt, Banker's Cheque, or Bank Guarantee. Note that Micro and Small Enterprises (MSEs) registered with designated bodies (Udyam Registration) and Startups recognized by DPIIT are exempted from submitting Bid Security (Rule 170(i)).
explanation_hindi: GFR 2017 के नियम 170 के अनुसार 'बोली सुरक्षा' (Bid Security / बयाना राशि - EMD) का प्रावधान गैर-गंभीर या लापरवाह बोलीदाताओं को बोली वैधता अवधि के दौरान हटने से रोकने के लिए किया जाता है। नियम 170 के तहत बोली सुरक्षा की राशि सामान्यतः खरीदे जाने वाले माल के अनुमानित मूल्य के 2% से 5% के बीच निर्धारित की जानी चाहिए। यह राशि अकाउंट पेयी डिमांड ड्राफ्ट, सावधि जमा रसीद (FDR), बैंकर चेक या बैंक गारंटी के रूप में स्वीकार की जा सकती है। उल्लेखनीय है कि सूक्ष्म एवं लघु उद्यमों (MSEs) तथा DPIIT द्वारा मान्यता प्राप्त स्टार्टअप्स को नियम 170(i) के तहत EMD जमा करने से छूट प्राप्त होती है।

question_english: Which of the following statements regarding "Performance Security" under Rule 171 of GFR 2017 is INCORRECT?
options_english: It is obtained from the successful bidder to guarantee the due and faithful performance of the contract.
It is standardly required to be an amount between 5% and 10% of the total value of the contract.

explanation_english:
Under Rule 171 of GFR 2017, Performance Security is obtained from the successful contractor to ensure satisfactory completion of contractual commitments. The rule establishes that:
1. Amount: Standardly 5% to 10% of the value of the contract (though temporarily adjusted during extraordinary fiscal periods by Ministry of Finance guidelines).
2. Validity: It must remain valid for a period of sixty (60) days beyond the date of completion of all contractual obligations of the supplier, including warranty obligations.
3. Form: It must be furnished in the form of an Account Payee Demand Draft, Fixed Deposit Receipt (FDR) pledged to the buyer, or a Bank Guarantee from a commercial bank (or online payment in an acceptable manner). Physical cash deposits in an institutional or school office are strictly prohibited under government accounting and treasury rules to ensure transparency and eliminate cash-handling risks.
explanation_hindi:
GFR 2017 के नियम 171 के अंतर्गत सफल आपूर्तिकर्ता से अनुबंध के संतोषजनक निष्पादन को सुनिश्चित करने हेतु 'परफॉर्मेंस सिक्योरिटी' ली जाती है। इसके मुख्य नियम निम्नलिखित हैं:
1. राशि: सामान्यतः अनुबंध के कुल मूल्य के 5% से 10% तक।
2. वैधता अवधि: आपूर्तिकर्ता के सभी संविदात्मक दायित्वों, जिसमें वारंटी अवधि भी शामिल है, के पूरा होने की तिथि के बाद 60 दिनों की अतिरिक्त अवधि तक वैध होनी चाहिए।
3. जमा करने का रूप: इसे अकाउंट पेयी डिमांड ड्राफ्ट, क्रेता के पक्ष में बंधक सावधि जमा रसीद (FDR) या वाणिज्यिक बैंक गारंटी के रूप में लिया जाता है। विद्यालय कार्यालय या किसी सरकारी कार्यालय में भौतिक नकदी (Cash) के रूप में इसे जमा कराना सरकारी लेखा एवं कोषागार नियमों के तहत सर्वथा निषिद्ध है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (C) It must be submitted exclusively in the form of physical cash deposited in the school office.

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: of physical cash deposited in the school office. Performance Security is collected from successful bidders to ensure satisfactory contract execution and warranty compliance. However, submitting performance security as physical cash deposited directly in an office is incorrect and prohibited under financial rules. Acceptable formats include account payee demand drafts, fixed deposit receipts, or bank guarantees, ensuring financial security through regulated banking channels.

question_english: A school Principal needs to procure a proprietary scientific apparatus that is manufactured exclusively by a single patent-holding firm. Under which specific provision of GFR 2017 is procurement from a single source permitted?
options_english: Rule 161 (Advertised Tender Enquiry)
Rule 162 (Limited Tender Enquiry)
Rule 154 (Purchase of goods without quotation)
Rule 166 (Single Tender Enquiry)
explanation_english: Rule 166 of GFR 2017 governs 'Single Tender Enquiry' (procurement from a single source). Procurement from a single source may be resorted to only under specific conditions: (i) It is in the knowledge of the user department that only a particular firm is the manufacturer of the required goods; (ii) In a case of emergency, the required goods are necessarily to be purchased from a particular source; or (iii) For standardization of machinery or spare parts to be compatible to the existing sets of equipments. When goods are proprietary to a single firm, the procuring official must record a mandatory 'Proprietary Article Certificate' (PAC) under Rule 166 before placing the order.
explanation_hindi: GFR 2017 का नियम 166 'एकल निविदा जांच' (Single Tender Enquiry) का नियमन करता है। एकल स्रोत से खरीद केवल विशेष परिस्थितियों में ही की जा सकती है: (i) जब उपभोक्ता विभाग की जानकारी में यह हो कि केवल एक ही विशिष्ट फर्म अपेक्षित माल की एकमात्र निर्माता (sole manufacturer) है; (ii) आपातकालीन स्थिति में जब किसी विशिष्ट स्रोत से ही खरीद अनिवार्य हो; या (iii) विद्यमान मशीनों के मानकीकरण या स्पेयर पार्ट्स की अनुकूलता हेतु। इस नियम के तहत खरीद करने के लिए सक्षम प्राधिकारी को निर्धारित प्रारूप में 'स्वामित्व वस्तु प्रमाण पत्र' (Proprietary Article Certificate - PAC) दर्ज करना अनिवार्य होता है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (D) Rule 166 (Single Tender Enquiry)

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Rule 166 of the General Financial Rules governs procurement through Single Tender Enquiry, which is applicable when required goods are manufactured solely by a proprietary firm or in cases of extreme emergency. To utilize this provision for proprietary equipment, the competent authority must record a formal Proprietary Article Certificate confirming that no alternative or equivalent product is suitable.

question_english: Under which Rule of GFR 2017 has the Government of India made it mandatory for all Ministries and subordinate offices to procure common-use goods and services through the Government e-Marketplace (GeM)?
options_english: Rule 149
Rule 130
Rule 144
Rule 154
explanation_english: Rule 149 of GFR 2017 specifically governs the 'Government e-Marketplace (GeM)'. The Ministry of Finance and the Government of India made procurement of common-use goods and services available on GeM mandatory for all Central Government Ministries, Departments, Subordinate/Attached offices, and Autonomous Bodies (including Kendriya Vidyalayas, Navodaya Vidyalayas, and Central Schools). The procuring authorities are required to verify the availability of items on GeM first, and only if an item is not available on GeM can offline procurement methods (Rules 154, 155, 161, 162) be resorted to, along with recording a Non-Availability Certificate (NAC) or justification.
explanation_hindi: GFR 2017 का नियम 149 विशेष रूप से 'गवर्नमेंट ई-मार्केटप्लेस' (GeM) से संबंधित है। वित्त मंत्रालय के आदेशानुसार सभी केंद्रीय मंत्रालयों, विभागों, उनके अधीनस्थ कार्यालयों तथा स्वायत्त निकायों (जैसे केंद्रीय विद्यालय, नवोदय विद्यालय आदि) के लिए GeM पर उपलब्ध सामान्य उपयोग की वस्तुओं और सेवाओं की खरीद GeM पोर्टल के माध्यम से करना वैधानिक रूप से अनिवार्य है। किसी भी ऑफलाइन खरीद (नियम 154, 155, 161 आदि) को अपनाने से पहले क्रेता को GeM पर वस्तु की अनुपलब्धता (Non-Availability Certificate) सुनिश्चित करनी होती है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) Rule 149

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Rule 149 of the General Financial Rules 2017 makes it mandatory for all central government ministries, departments, and subordinate offices to procure common-use goods and services through the online Government e-Marketplace (GeM). This statutory requirement aims to drive digital governance, consolidate government purchasing power, streamline administrative workflows, and eliminate manual procurement inefficiencies across public offices.

question_hindi: GFR 2017 के नियम 149 के परिचालन प्रावधानों के अनुसार, कोई सरकारी क्रेता GeM पोर्टल पर अपेक्षित गुणवत्ता, विनिर्देश और वितरण अवधि को पूरा करने वाले किसी भी उपलब्ध विक्रेता से सीधे ऑनलाइन खरीद किस वित्तीय सीमा तक कर सकता है?

question_english: According to the operational provisions of Rule 149 of GFR 2017, up to what financial ceiling can a government buyer make a direct online purchase on GeM from any available seller meeting the required quality, specification, and delivery period?
options_english: Up to Rs. 50,000/-
Up to Rs. 25,000/-
explanation_english:
Rule 149 of GFR 2017 prescribes the financial thresholds for procurement on the Government e-Marketplace (GeM):
1. Up to Rs. 25,000/-: Direct online purchase can be made from any available seller on GeM who meets the requisite quality, specification, and delivery period (without mandatory comparison of multiple sellers).
2. Above Rs. 25,000/- and up to Rs. 5,00,000/-: Purchase is to be made through the seller offering the lowest price (L1) after comparing at least three different manufacturers/sellers on GeM meeting identical specifications.
3. Above Rs. 5,00,000/-: Mandatory procurement through online bidding or reverse auction tool provided on GeM.
Therefore, the direct purchase limit from any single seller meeting requirements without comparison under Rule 149(i) is up to Rs. 25,000/-.
explanation_hindi:
GFR 2017 के नियम 149 के अंतर्गत GeM पोर्टल के माध्यम से खरीद के लिए निम्नलिखित वित्तीय सीमाएं निर्धारित हैं:
1. ₹25,000/- तक: क्रेता GeM पर उपलब्ध किसी भी ऐसे विक्रेता से सीधे ऑनलाइन खरीद कर सकता है जो अपेक्षित गुणवत्ता, तकनीकी विनिर्देश और आपूर्ति अवधि को पूरा करता हो (बिना किसी तुलनात्मक बोली के)।
2. ₹25,000/- से अधिक और ₹5,00,000/- तक: GeM पर समान विनिर्देशों वाले कम से कम तीन अलग-अलग निर्माताओं/विक्रेताओं के बीच ऑनलाइन तुलना करने के बाद सबसे कम मूल्य (L1) देने वाले विक्रेता से खरीद की जाती है।
3. ₹5,00,000/- से अधिक: GeM पर अनिवार्य रूप से ऑनलाइन बोली (bidding) या रिवर्स ऑक्शन (reverse auction) के माध्यम से खरीद की जानी चाहिए।
अतः बिना तुलना के सीधे खरीद की अधिकतम सीमा ₹25,000/- है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (B) Up to Rs. 25,000/-

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Under the operational provisions of Rule 149 on the Government e-Marketplace portal, direct online purchases can be executed for common- use items valued up to twenty-five thousand rupees. The buyer can select any registered seller meeting basic requisite quality, technical specification, and delivery timeline parameters without conducting price comparisons or formal online bidding processes.

question_hindi:
गवर्नमेंट ई-मार्केटप्लेस (GeM) पर खरीद सीमाओं (वित्तीय सीमाओं) के संबंध में निम्नलिखित कथनों पर विचार कीजिए:
I. ₹25,000 तक की खरीद GeM पर उपलब्ध किसी भी आपूर्तिकर्ता के माध्यम से की जा सकती है, बशर्ते वह वांछित गुणवत्ता, विनिर्देश और वितरण अवधि को पूरा करता हो।
II. ₹25,000 से अधिक और ₹5,00,000 तक की खरीद कम से कम तीन विभिन्न निर्माताओं के उपलब्ध विक्रेताओं में से सबसे कम मूल्य वाले (L1) विक्रेता के माध्यम से की जानी चाहिए।
III. ₹5,00,000 से अधिक की खरीद के लिए GeM पर ऑनलाइन बिडिंग (बोली) या ई-रिवर्स ऑक्शन अनिवार्य है।
IV. केंद्र सरकार के मंत्रालयों और विभागों के लिए GeM के माध्यम से खरीद करना वैकल्पिक (ऐच्छिक) है।
उपर्युक्त कथनों में से कौन-से सही हैं?

subject: UPSC Principal Paper
question_english:
Consider the following statements regarding procurement limits on the Government e-Marketplace (GeM):
I. Purchases up to Rs. 25,000 can be made through any of the available suppliers on GeM meeting the requisite quality, specification, and delivery period.
II. Purchases above Rs. 25,000 and up to Rs. 5,00,000 should be made through the L1 (lowest) bidder among available suppliers of at least three different manufacturers.
III. Purchases above Rs. 5,00,000 mandatorily require online bidding or reverse auction on GeM.
IV. Procurement through GeM is optional for Ministries and Departments of the Central Government.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
options_english: I, II and III
I, III and IV
II, III and IV
I, II, III and IV
explanation_english:
Under Rule 149 of the General Financial Rules (GFR), 2017, procurement of common-use goods and services through the Government e-Marketplace (GeM) is mandatory, not optional, for all Central Government Ministries, Departments, and attached/subordinate offices, including educational institutions like Kendriya Vidyalayas and Navodaya Vidyalayas. Rule 149 prescribes strict threshold-based procurement procedures:
1. Direct Purchase (Up to Rs. 25,000): The buyer can procure directly from any available supplier on GeM whose product meets requisite quality, technical specifications, and delivery period.
2. L1 Comparison (Above Rs. 25,000 up to Rs. 5,00,000): The buyer must compare available products from at least three different manufacturers on GeM and select the lowest cost (L1) bidder that satisfies technical requirements.
3. Mandatory Online Bidding / e-Reverse Auction (Above Rs. 5,00,000): The procurement must mandatorily be conducted through online bidding or reverse auction tools integrated into GeM.
Because GeM is statutory and mandatory under GFR Rule 149, Statement IV is incorrect. Statements I, II, and III are correct.
explanation_hindi:
सामान्य वित्तीय नियम (GFR), 2017 के नियम 149 के अनुसार, केंद्र सरकार के सभी मंत्रालयों, विभागों तथा उनके अधीनस्थ कार्यालयों (जिनमें केंद्रीय विद्यालय एवं नवोदय विद्यालय जैसे स्वायत्त निकाय भी शामिल हैं) के लिए GeM (गवर्नमेंट ई-मार्केटप्लेस) पर उपलब्ध सामान्य उपयोग की वस्तुओं और सेवाओं की खरीद करना अनिवार्य है, न कि वैकल्पिक। नियम 149 के अंतर्गत वित्तीय सीमाएं इस प्रकार निर्धारित हैं:
1. ₹25,000 तक: वांछित गुणवत्ता, तकनीकी विनिर्देश और वितरण अवधि को पूरा करने वाले GeM पर उपलब्ध किसी भी विक्रेता से सीधी खरीद की जा सकती है।
2. ₹25,000 से अधिक तथा ₹5,00,000 तक: GeM पर उपलब्ध कम से कम तीन अलग-अलग निर्माताओं के उत्पादों की तुलना करके सबसे कम मूल्य (L1) वाले योग्य विक्रेता का चयन करना अनिवार्य है।
3. ₹5,00,000 से अधिक: GeM पर उपलब्ध ऑनलाइन बिडिंग (बोली) या ई-रिवर्स ऑक्शन (e-Reverse Auction) उपकरण के माध्यम से ही खरीद की जानी अनिवार्य है।
चूंकि GeM से खरीद करना मंत्रालयों/विभागों के लिए अनिवार्य है, अतः कथन IV गलत है। कथन I, II और III सही हैं।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) I, II and III

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: GeM rules establish structured purchase thresholds: direct purchase up to twenty-five thousand rupees, mandatory comparison among at least three different manufacturers to select the lowest bidder for values up to five lakh rupees, and mandatory online bidding or reverse auction above five lakh rupees. Crucially, GeM procurement is mandatory, not optional, for central government entities.

question_english: A school Principal urgently requires 10 whiteboards for newly constructed classrooms, with a total estimated cost of Rs. 35,000. Under the provisions of GFR 2017, how should the Principal proceed to procure these whiteboards through GeM?
options_english: By comparing prices of at least three different GeM manufacturers and selecting the L1 bidder
By directly selecting any random registered seller offering whiteboards on the portal
By calling a physical open tender outside GeM since the purchase amount exceeds Rs. 25,000
By purchasing the required items from the local market directly without verifying GeM availability
explanation_english: According to Rule 149(ii) of GFR 2017, for procurement of goods valued between Rs. 25,000 and Rs. 5,00,000 on the Government e-Marketplace (GeM), the purchasing authority (Head of Office / Principal / DDO) must mandate an online comparison of products from at least three different manufacturers available on the portal. The buyer must verify that the products meet the required technical specifications, warranty, and delivery schedule, and then award the purchase order to the lowest-priced (L1) qualified bidder. Because the estimated procurement value of the whiteboards is Rs. 35,000, it falls within the Rs. 25,000 to Rs. 5,00,000 threshold. The Principal cannot bypass this comparison to make a direct single-seller purchase (permitted only up to Rs. 25,000), nor bypass GeM to purchase locally without a Non-Availability Certificate.
explanation_hindi: GFR 2017 के नियम 149(ii) के अनुसार, गवर्नमेंट ई-मार्केटप्लेस (GeM) पर ₹25,000 से अधिक और ₹5,00,000 तक की वस्तुओं की खरीद के लिए, क्रय प्राधिकारी (कार्यालय प्रमुख / विद्यालय प्राचार्य / DDO) को पोर्टल पर उपलब्ध कम से कम तीन अलग-अलग निर्माताओं के उत्पादों के विनिर्देशों और मूल्यों की ऑनलाइन तुलना करना अनिवार्य है। इसके उपरांत निर्धारित तकनीकी विनिर्देशों को पूरा करने वाले न्यूनतम मूल्य बोलीदाता (L1) को खरीद आदेश जारी किया जाना चाहिए। चूंकि 10 व्हाइटबोर्ड की अनुमानित लागत ₹35,000 है, यह ₹25,000 से ₹5,00,000 की श्रेणी में आती है। प्राचार्य किसी एक विक्रेता से सीधे खरीद नहीं कर सकते (सीधी खरीद केवल ₹25,000 तक मान्य है), और न ही GeM को नजरअंदाज करके खुले बाजार या बाहरी खुली निविदा का सहारा ले सकते हैं।

question_english:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).
Assertion (A): It is mandatory for all Ministries and Departments to procure goods and services available on GeM through the portal.
Reason (R): GeM has been developed to enhance transparency, efficiency, and speed in public procurement.
In light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options_english: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is true but (R) is false
(A) is false but (R) is true
explanation_english: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, and (R) provides the correct explanation of (A). Under Rule 149 of the General Financial Rules (GFR), 2017, the Government of India made procurement of common-use goods and services available on GeM mandatory for all Central Ministries, Departments, and attached/autonomous bodies. The fundamental objective behind developing and mandating GeM was to completely overhaul traditional public procurement by introducing a unified, contactless, paperless, and cashless digital platform that enhances public expenditure transparency, ensures competitive fair pricing, prevents cartelization and corruption, and drastically improves procurement processing speed. Hence, Reason (R) correctly explains the mandate in Assertion (A).
explanation_hindi: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं तथा कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या प्रस्तुत करता है। सामान्य वित्तीय नियम (GFR), 2017 के नियम 149 के अनुसार, केंद्र सरकार के सभी मंत्रालयों और विभागों के लिए GeM पोर्टल पर उपलब्ध सामान्य उपयोग की वस्तुओं और सेवाओं को GeM के माध्यम से ही खरीदना कानूनी रूप से अनिवार्य है। केंद्र सरकार द्वारा GeM को विकसित करने और इसे अनिवार्य बनाने का मुख्य उद्देश्य सार्वजनिक खरीद में पूर्ण पारदर्शिता, कार्यकुशलता, वित्तीय मितव्ययिता और गतिशीलता लाना था ताकि बिचौलियों, भ्रष्टाचार और कागजी निविदाओं की जटिलताओं को समाप्त किया जा सके और सरकारी धन का सर्वोत्तम उपयोग सुनिश्चित हो सके। अतः कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) का सही और तार्किक स्पष्टीकरण है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: correct explanation of (A) Central government entities are legally required to procure available goods and services through the Government e-Marketplace. The primary objective driving this mandate is to leverage an integrated digital platform that enhances public procurement transparency, ensures competitive pricing, accelerates transaction speed, and minimizes manual intervention, thereby ensuring greater accountability in public expenditure management.

question_english: Identify the correct statement regarding the responsibility for the quality of goods procured through GeM:
options_english: The Principal Accounts Office holds sole financial and technical responsibility for verifying quality of goods.
GeM administration holds sole legal and operational responsibility for the physical quality of delivered goods.
The State Government Finance Department guarantees the quality and specification of all goods listed on GeM.
Responsibility for quality, specifications, and timely delivery lies with the buyer.
explanation_english: Under Rule 149 of GFR 2017 and the GeM General Terms and Conditions (GTC), the Government e-Marketplace serves as a digital transaction platform connecting government buyers with registered sellers, but the ultimate responsibility for verifying the quality, conformity to technical specifications, and timely receipt of goods rests solely with the Buyer (the procuring department, school Principal, or DDO). Upon receiving consignments, the buyer/consignee is legally obligated to inspect the goods physically and generate a Consignee Receipt and Acceptance Certificate (CRAC) on the portal within the prescribed timeline (normally 10 days) before payment is released. Neither GeM administration nor the Accounts Office physically inspects or guarantees the delivered products.
explanation_hindi: GFR 2017 के नियम 149 और GeM के सामान्य नियमों और शर्तों (GTC) के अनुसार, गवर्नमेंट ई-मार्केटप्लेस केवल एक ऑनलाइन तकनीकी मंच है जो सरकारी खरीदारों को विक्रेताओं से जोड़ता है। परंतु आपूर्ति की गई वस्तुओं के तकनीकी विनिर्देशों (specifications), भौतिक गुणवत्ता, मात्रा और समय पर वितरण की जांच करने की संपूर्ण जिम्मेदारी क्रेता (कार्यालय प्रमुख / विद्यालय प्राचार्य / DDO) की होती है। वस्तुओं की प्राप्ति पर, कंसाइनी/क्रेता को भौतिक निरीक्षण करना होता है और निर्धारित समय सीमा (सामान्यतः 10 कार्यदिवस) के भीतर GeM पोर्टल पर 'कंसाइनी प्राप्ति और स्वीकृति प्रमाण पत्र' (CRAC) जारी करना होता है, जिसके बाद ही विक्रेता को भुगतान किया जाता है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (D) Responsibility for quality, specifications, and timely delivery lies with the buyer.

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: timely delivery lies with the buyer. Although the Government e-Marketplace platform provides an online catalog and registered seller directory, the ultimate responsibility for verifying product quality, ensuring technical specifications meet operational requirements, and confirming timely delivery rests entirely with the buyer. Receiving authorities must inspect all delivered goods and issue online acceptance certificates before releasing payment to vendors.

question_english: In which of the following exceptional circumstances can an authority bypass GeM for procuring common-use goods?
options_english: When goods are available on GeM but a local vendor offers a significant promotional cash discount.
When the buyer's procurement committee finds that the online e-marketplace platform is complex to navigate.
When a certificate of non-availability (GeM Availability Report) is generated on the portal.
When the total procurement proposal value falls below the minimal threshold of Rs. 1,000 per occasion.
explanation_english: Under Rule 149 of GFR 2017 and Ministry of Finance (Department of Expenditure) guidelines, procuring common-use goods and services available on GeM through open-market channels outside GeM is strictly prohibited. Bypassing GeM is legally permissible only when the specific required item or service is genuinely not available on GeM, or when the available products do not meet mandatory technical specifications. In such situations, the procuring entity must perform a search on the GeM portal and generate a system-certified 'GeM Availability Report' (Certificate of Non-Availability) with a unique GeM AR ID. Only after recording this certificate on file can the department proceed to procure through alternative routes such as Rule 154 (Direct Purchase without Quotation) or Rule 155 (Local Purchase Committee).
explanation_hindi: GFR 2017 के नियम 149 और वित्त मंत्रालय (व्यय विभाग) के दिशा-निर्देशों के अनुसार, GeM पर उपलब्ध सामान्य उपयोग की वस्तुओं और सेवाओं को GeM के बाहर खुले बाजार से खरीदना पूरी तरह से प्रतिबंधित है। GeM को छोड़कर बाह्य माध्यमों से खरीद करने की अनुमति केवल तभी है जब वांछित वस्तु या सेवा GeM पोर्टल पर उपलब्ध न हो। इस असाधारण परिस्थिति में, क्रेता को पोर्टल पर सर्च करके आधिकारिक 'GeM उपलब्धता रिपोर्ट' (गैर-उपलब्धता प्रमाण पत्र / GeM Availability Report) उत्पन्न करनी होती है, जिसका एक विशिष्ट आईडी नंबर होता है। इस प्रमाण पत्र को फाइल में दर्ज करने के बाद ही विभाग GFR नियम 154 या 155 के तहत बाह्य खरीद प्रक्रिया प्रारंभ कर सकता है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (C) When a certificate of non-availability (GeM Availability Report) is generated on the portal.

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Availability Report) is generated on the portal. Bypassing the mandatory online e-marketplace platform to procure common-use goods through outside channels is permissible only when the specific required item or service is unavailable on the portal. In such instances, the procuring entity must generate an official non-availability report directly from the portal, documenting the unavailability before initiating alternative external procurement processes.

question_english: What is a primary technological feature of GeM designed to ensure competitiveness and fair pricing for high-value procurements?
options_english: Manual sealed envelopes submitted by post
E-reverse auction
Telephonic negotiation with local vendors
Direct advance payments to preferred vendors
explanation_english: Under Rule 149(iii) of the General Financial Rules (GFR), 2017, for procurements exceeding Rs. 5,00,000, buyers must mandatorily conduct online bidding or an electronic reverse auction on GeM. An electronic reverse auction (e-RA) is a dynamic online pricing mechanism where technically qualified sellers compete against each other in real-time during a scheduled electronic auction window, offering progressively lower prices. This transparent and automated competition prevents supplier collusion, removes human discretion or manual negotiations, and secures the most economical market prices for the government exchequer.
explanation_hindi: सामान्य वित्तीय नियम (GFR), 2017 के नियम 149(iii) के अनुसार, ₹5,00,000 से अधिक की खरीद के लिए GeM पोर्टल पर ऑनलाइन बिडिंग या इलेक्ट्रॉनिक रिवर्स ऑक्शन (e-Reverse Auction) का उपयोग करना अनिवार्य है। ई-रिवर्स ऑक्शन एक गतिशील ऑनलाइन नीलामी प्रणाली है जिसमें तकनीकी रूप से योग्य विक्रेता एक निर्धारित समय-सीमा के दौरान वास्तविक समय (real-time) में एक-दूसरे के विरुद्ध प्रतिस्पर्धी बोलियां लगाते हुए अपने मूल्यों को घटाते हैं। यह स्वचालित और पारदर्शी तंत्र आपूर्तिकर्ताओं के गठजोड़ को समाप्त करता है, मानवीय बातचीत को रोकता है और सरकारी खजाने के लिए न्यूनतम और सर्वाधिक प्रतिस्पर्धी मूल्य सुनिश्चित करता है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (B) E-reverse auction

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: To maximize cost efficiency and foster dynamic competition for high-value procurements, the Government e-Marketplace incorporates an electronic reverse auction feature. This technology enables pre-qualified vendors to submit real-time, progressively lower price bids online during a specified timeframe, driving market prices down through automated transparent competition and delivering significant savings to the government treasury.

question_english: Which of the following best describes the primary advantage of utilizing GeM in school administration?
options_english: It completely eliminates the administrative requirement for maintaining a physical or digital stock register in the school office.
It empowers the Head of School to sanction and spend unlimited government funds without prior budget provisions or allocations.
It automatically awards schools with additional direct state developmental grants based on their annual procurement transaction volume.
It reduces administrative burden of tendering and ensures compliance with procurement rules.
explanation_english: The primary operational and administrative advantage of utilizing GeM in school administration is that it eliminates cumbersome paper-based tender publishing, physical advertisement costs, manual bid openings, and extensive comparative statement preparation, while guaranteeing automated compliance with public procurement rules (GFR Rule 149). The other statements are incorrect: (1) maintaining physical or digital stock registers is strictly required under GFR Rules 209 and 211, (2) financial delegation limits and prior budget availability under Rule 8 and Rule 10 of DFPR remain mandatory on Heads of Schools / DDOs, and (3) GeM does not grant additional development grants based on procurement volumes.
explanation_hindi: विद्यालय प्रशासन में GeM के उपयोग का सबसे बड़ा प्रशासनिक लाभ यह है कि यह पारंपरिक कागजी निविदाओं को प्रकाशित करने, समाचार पत्रों के विज्ञापनों, भौतिक बोलियां प्राप्त करने और लंबी फाइलों के रखरखाव के भारी प्रशासनिक बोझ को समाप्त करता है, तथा GFR नियम 149 के तहत वित्तीय नियमों का पूर्ण अनुपालन सुनिश्चित करता है। अन्य विकल्प गलत हैं क्योंकि: (1) GFR 2017 के नियम 209 और 211 के तहत विद्यालय में स्टॉक रजिस्टर बनाए रखना अभी भी पूर्णतः अनिवार्य है, (2) DDO और प्राचार्य वित्तीय शक्तियों के प्रत्यायोजन नियमों (DFPR) और स्वीकृत बजट सीमा के भीतर ही व्यय कर सकते हैं, और (3) GeM खरीद की मात्रा के आधार पर कोई अतिरिक्त विकासात्मक अनुदान नहीं देता है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (D) It reduces administrative burden of tendering and ensures compliance with procurement rules.

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: and ensures compliance with procurement rules. Utilizing the Government e-Marketplace streamlines institutional administration by eliminating time-consuming manual tender drafting, physical advertisement, and paper evaluation procedures. It offers a standardized, rule-compliant online workflow that ensures full adherence to general financial guidelines, reduces administrative delays in acquiring necessary operational supplies, and provides verified commercial options for educational institutional needs.

Domestic commercial services and International services
Primary administrative services and Secondary services
Direct operational services and Indirect services
explanation_english:
Under Chapter 6 of the General Financial Rules (GFR), 2017, the procurement of services is bifurcated into two distinct categories:
1. Consulting Services (Rules 177 to 196): Covers assignments of an intellectual, technical, or advisory nature where specialized professional knowledge and expertise are procured (e.g., policy formulation, feasibility studies, engineering design, architectural consulting, legal counsel).
2. Non-Consulting Services (Rules 197 to 206): Covers physical, measurable, operational, or maintenance activities where measurable physical performance, labor, equipment, or materials predominate over specialized intellectual advice (e.g., security guard deployment, sanitation, catering, transportation, IT hardware maintenance).
explanation_hindi:
सामान्य वित्तीय नियम (GFR), 2017 के अध्याय 6 के अंतर्गत सेवाओं की खरीद को दो प्रमुख श्रेणियों में विभाजित किया गया है:
1. परामर्श सेवाएं (Consulting Services - नियम 177 से 196): इसमें बौद्धिक, तकनीकी अथवा सलाहकारी प्रकृति के कार्य शामिल हैं जिनमें विशेष व्यावसायिक ज्ञान एवं विशेषज्ञता की आवश्यकता होती है (जैसे परियोजना अध्ययन, वास्तुशिल्प डिजाइन, कानूनी सलाह आदि)।
2. गैर-परामर्श सेवाएं (Non-Consulting Services - नियम 197 से 206): इसमें ऐसी भौतिक, परिचालन संबंधी अथवा नियमित रखरखाव वाली गतिविधियां शामिल हैं जिनमें श्रम, मशीनरी अथवा भौतिक प्रदर्शन की प्रधानता होती है और जिनके परिणामों को मापने योग्य इकाइयों में आंका जा सकता है (जैसे सुरक्षा सेवाएं, साफ-सफाई, खानपान, परिवहन सेवाएं आदि)।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) Consulting services and Non-consulting services

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: services The General Financial Rules classify service procurement into two broad categories: consulting services and non-consulting services. Consulting services involve specialized intellectual, advisory, or professional expertise provided by qualified firms or individuals. Non-consulting services involve physical, operational, or routine measurable activities where labor, equipment, or physical performance dominates over specialized professional advice.

Preparation of a detailed project report by an architect
Outsourcing of cleaning, security, and catering services
Legal counsel for a complex litigation
explanation_english: As defined in Rule 197 of GFR 2017, 'Non-consulting services' involve operational, physical, maintenance, or routine measurable activities where labor, equipment, physical inputs, or standard performance indicators dominate rather than customized intellectual or professional advice. Common examples include outsourcing office sanitation and housekeeping, physical security guarding, canteen/catering operations, hiring of motor vehicles, and courier services. Conversely, management advisory services, detailed architectural project reports (DPR), and specialized legal counsel are intellectual, professional, and advisory tasks classified as 'Consulting Services' under Rule 177 of GFR 2017.

question_english:
Consider the following statements regarding the procurement of Consulting Services:
I. A specialized firm or expert is engaged for services requiring intellectual or professional input.
II. Preparation of Terms of Reference (ToR) is a mandatory first step.
III. Consulting services can only be procured if the required expertise is abundantly available within the department itself.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
options_english: I and II
II and III
I and III
I, II and III
explanation_english:
Statements I and II are correct, while Statement III is incorrect:
- Statement I is correct: Rule 177 of GFR 2017 defines consulting services as specialized intellectual, technical, or advisory services rendered by expert firms or individuals.
- Statement II is correct: Under Rule 185 of GFR 2017, drafting a comprehensive Terms of Reference (ToR) is the mandatory starting point of consulting procurement. The ToR defines the assignment background, precise objectives, detailed scope of work, timelines, and deliverables.
- Statement III is incorrect: Rule 178 of GFR 2017 clearly provides that consulting services should be engaged only when the required specialized expertise is NOT available in-house within the Ministry or Department, or when in-house resources are inadequate to complete the assignment within required timeframes. Engaging external consultants when expertise already exists in-house is financially unjustified and prohibited.
explanation_hindi:
कथन I और II सही हैं, जबकि कथन III गलत है:
- कथन I सही है: GFR 2017 का नियम 177 परामर्श सेवाओं को उन विशिष्ट बौद्धिक, तकनीकी अथवा सलाहकारी सेवाओं के रूप में परिभाषित करता है जो योग्य सलाहकारों या विशेषज्ञ फर्मों द्वारा प्रदान की जाती हैं।
- कथन II सही है: नियम 185 के तहत कार्य संदर्भ (Terms of Reference - ToR) तैयार करना परामर्श सेवाओं की खरीद का अनिवार्य प्रथम चरण है, जिसमें कार्य का दायरा, उद्देश्य, तकनीकी आवश्यकताएं और डिलिवरेबल्स स्पष्ट रूप से निर्धारित होते हैं।
- कथन III गलत है: नियम 178 यह स्पष्ट रूप से रेखांकित करता है कि किसी विभाग को परामर्श सेवाएं केवल तभी लेनी चाहिए जब संबंधित तकनीकी या व्यावसायिक विशेषज्ञता विभाग के पास आंतरिक रूप से उपलब्ध न हो। यदि विशेषज्ञता विभाग के भीतर ही प्रचुर मात्रा में उपलब्ध है, तो बाहरी सलाहकारों पर सरकारी धन व्यय करना अनुचित और वित्तीय नियमों के विरुद्ध है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) I and II

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Engaging consulting services is appropriate when an organization requires specialized intellectual, technical, or professional expertise not available internally. Preparing comprehensive Terms of Reference is a mandatory initial step to define clear objectives and deliverables. If required expertise is already abundantly available within the department, engaging external private consultants is unnecessary and economically unjustified.

question_english: The Directorate of Education directs a school Principal to hire private security guards to secure the school premises. What process must the Principal follow under GFR for procuring this non-consulting service?
options_english: Directly engage security personnel from the local neighborhood and pay monthly remuneration in physical cash.
Submit a formal request to the local police station to station free security guards at the school indefinitely.
Directly nominate a private security agency personally known to the SMC members without inviting competitive bids.
Use GeM for outsourcing non-consulting security services per financial limits.
explanation_english: Under GFR 2017 (Rules 149 and 197 to 206), private watch-and-ward/security guard deployment is categorized as a 'Non-Consulting Service'. Because security services are standardized and readily available on the Government e-Marketplace (GeM), institutional heads (Principals / DDOs) must mandatorily procure them through GeM in compliance with prescribed financial thresholds, service-level agreements (SLAs), and statutory minimum wage compliance. Direct nomination of local acquaintances, cash disbursements, or bypassing competitive bidding violates Rule 144, Rule 149, and Central Vigilance Commission (CVC) guidelines governing public service contracts.
explanation_hindi: GFR 2017 (नियम 149 तथा नियम 197 से 206) के तहत निजी सुरक्षा गार्डों की तैनाती एक 'गैर-परामर्श सेवा' (Non-Consulting Service) है। चूंकि GeM पोर्टल पर सुरक्षा सेवाएं मानकीकृत रूप से उपलब्ध हैं, इसलिए विद्यालय प्राचार्य (कार्यालय प्रमुख/DDO) को निर्धारित वित्तीय सीमाओं, सेवा स्तर समझौतों (SLA) और वैधानिक न्यूनतम वेतन नियमों का पालन करते हुए GeM के माध्यम से ही इस सेवा को आउटसोर्स करना अनिवार्य है। बिना निविदा के परिचितों को काम सौंपना, नकद भुगतान करना या खुली प्रतिस्पर्धा को दरकिनार करना GFR और केंद्रीय सतर्कता आयोग (CVC) के नियमों का प्रत्यक्ष उल्लंघन है।

question_english: Which of the following is INCORRECT regarding the preparation of the Terms of Reference (ToR) for hiring a consultant?
options_english: It should clearly define the precise objective, detailed scope, and specific tasks of the assignment.
It should pre-select the desired firm and tailor requirements to match only that firm.
It must comprehensively detail all the expected physical and financial deliverables and timelines.
It should outline the organizational background, rationale, and core purpose of the assignment.
explanation_english: Statement B is incorrect and describes a prohibited corrupt practice. Under Rule 185 of GFR 2017, the Terms of Reference (ToR) must provide an objective, transparent, and comprehensive description of the background, objectives, scope of work, tasks, training requirements, and expected deliverables with timeframes. Rule 144 (Fundamental Principles of Public Buying) strictly forbids formulating technical criteria or ToR in a manner that favors a particular bidder or restricts open competition. Tailoring requirements to pre-select a specific consulting firm undermines public procurement transparency, fair competition, and accountability.
explanation_hindi: कथन B गलत है और यह एक निषिद्ध तथा भ्रष्ट आचरण को दर्शाता है। GFR 2017 के नियम 185 के अनुसार, कार्य संदर्भ (ToR) में परियोजना की पृष्ठभूमि, उद्देश्य, कार्य का दायरा, विशिष्ट कार्य, समय-सीमा और अपेक्षित डिलिवरेबल्स का निष्पक्ष और वस्तुनिष्ठ विवरण होना चाहिए। नियम 144 (सार्वजनिक खरीद के मौलिक सिद्धांत) के अनुसार निविदा या ToR की शर्तें कभी भी इस प्रकार नहीं बनाई जानी चाहिए जो किसी विशिष्ट फर्म या बोलीदाता के पक्ष में हों या खुली प्रतिस्पर्धा को सीमित करती हों। किसी विशेष फर्म को लाभ पहुंचाने के उद्देश्य से शर्तों को पक्षपातपूर्ण बनाना वित्तीय नियमों और CVC दिशानिर्देशों का गंभीर उल्लंघन है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (B) It should pre-select the desired firm and tailor requirements to match only that firm.

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: tailor requirements to match only that firm. The Terms of Reference must outline the background, objectives, scope of work, technical parameters, timelines, and expected deliverables for a consulting engagement. Tailoring requirements to match or pre-select a specific firm is strictly prohibited, as it undermines fair competition and transparency. Specifications must remain objective to encourage broad participation from qualified consultants.

question_english:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).
Assertion (A): For the selection of consultants, the Quality and Cost Based Selection (QCBS) method is frequently used.
Reason (R): The QCBS method allows the procuring entity to evaluate bids based only on the lowest cost, ignoring the technical competence of the consultant.
In light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options_english: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is true but (R) is false
(A) is false but (R) is true
explanation_english:
Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false:
- Assertion (A) is true: Under Rule 192 of GFR 2017, Quality and Cost Based Selection (QCBS) is the standard and most widely utilized method for selecting consultants, especially when the quality of the assignment is paramount and balanced against cost.
- Reason (R) is false: QCBS does NOT evaluate bids based solely on lowest cost, nor does it ignore technical competence. On the contrary, under QCBS, proposals are evaluated based on combined technical and financial scores with predetermined weightages (typically 80% for technical quality and 20% for cost, or 70:30). The bidder obtaining the highest combined score is awarded the contract. Evaluating bids solely on lowest financial cost after minimal qualification is the 'Least Cost System' (LCS) under Rule 193, not QCBS.
Therefore, (A) is true but (R) is false.
explanation_hindi:
अभिकथन (A) सही है, परंतु कारण (R) गलत है:
- अभिकथन (A) सही है: GFR 2017 के नियम 192 के तहत, गुणवत्ता और लागत आधारित चयन (QCBS) परामर्श सेवाओं के चयन के लिए सर्वाधिक उपयोग की जाने वाली प्रणाली है, जहाँ बौद्धिक आउटपुट की गुणवत्ता और वित्तीय लागत दोनों का संतुलित मूल्यांकन किया जाता है।
- कारण (R) गलत है: QCBS में तकनीकी योग्यता की अनदेखी नहीं की जाती और न ही चयन केवल न्यूनतम लागत के आधार पर होता है। इसके विपरीत, QCBS में तकनीकी प्रस्ताव और वित्तीय प्रस्ताव दोनों का मूल्यांकन पूर्व-निर्धारित भारांक (जैसे 80% तकनीकी और 20% वित्तीय) देकर किया जाता है। दोनों को मिलाकर सर्वाधिक संयुक्त अंक (highest combined score) प्राप्त करने वाले बोलीदाता को अनुबंध दिया जाता है। न्यूनतम लागत पर चयन की प्रणाली 'न्यूनतम लागत प्रणाली' (LCS - नियम 193) कहलाती है। अतः (A) सही है लेकिन (R) गलत है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (C) (A) is true but (R) is false

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Quality and Cost Based Selection is a widely utilized methodology for evaluating consulting proposals. However, it does not evaluate bids based solely on cost. Instead, it assigns weightage to both technical competence and financial proposals, balancing technical capability with competitive pricing. This ensures high-quality intellectual output while maintaining reasonable expenditure controls.

question_english: Under Rule 194 of GFR 2017, up to what estimated value can a Ministry or Department procure consulting services on a nomination basis in cases of extreme urgency, with the approval of the competent authority?
options_english: Up to Rs. 50,000
Up to Rs. 1 Lakh
Up to Rs. 10 Lakhs
Up to Rs. 2.5 Lakhs
explanation_english:
Under Rule 194 of the General Financial Rules (GFR), 2017 ('Procurement of Consulting services by nomination'), single-source selection or engagement of a consultant on a nomination basis without open competitive bidding is an exception strictly restricted to special circumstances, such as:
(i) In situations of extreme urgency or emergency, or
(ii) When only a particular consulting firm has exclusive technical ownership or intellectual capability.
Rule 194 specifically provides that in cases of emergency, a Ministry or Department may procure consulting services on a direct nomination basis up to an estimated value of Rs. 2.5 Lakhs (Rupees Two Lakhs and Fifty Thousand only) per occasion, subject to detailed recorded justifications and the prior approval of the competent authority / Head of Department.

question_english:
Arrange the following steps for the procurement of consulting services in the correct order:
I. Invitation for Expression of Interest (EoI)
II. Preparation of Terms of Reference (ToR)
III. Shortlisting of consultants
IV. Evaluation of Technical and Financial bids
options_english: II, I, III, IV
I, II, III, IV
II, III, I, IV
I, III, II, IV
explanation_english:
Under Chapter 6 (Procurement of Services) of GFR 2017, the sequential stages for procuring consulting services follow a prescribed legal hierarchy:
1. Step II: Preparation of Terms of Reference (ToR) (Rule 185) - Formulating the foundational document specifying the project background, objectives, scope of work, and expected deliverables.
2. Step I: Invitation for Expression of Interest (EoI) (Rule 186) - Publishing an open notice (mandatory for estimated costs exceeding Rs. 25 Lakhs) to invite expressions of interest from competent consulting firms.
3. Step III: Shortlisting of Consultants (Rule 187) - Evaluating EoI submissions against pre-announced criteria and shortlisting a manageable number of qualified firms (normally 3 to 8).
4. Step IV: Issue of Request for Proposals (RFP) & Evaluation of Technical and Financial Bids (Rules 188 to 193) - Inviting detailed proposals from shortlisted firms, conducting two-stage bid evaluations, and selecting the successful consultant.
Therefore, the correct chronological order is II -> I -> III -> IV.
explanation_hindi:
GFR 2017 के अध्याय 6 (सेवाओं की खरीद) के अनुसार परामर्श सेवाओं की खरीद के चरणों का सही वैधानिक क्रम इस प्रकार है:
1. चरण II: कार्य संदर्भ (Terms of Reference - ToR) तैयार करना (नियम 185) - यह आधारभूत दस्तावेज है जिसमें परियोजना के उद्देश्य, कार्य का दायरा और डिलिवरेबल्स निर्धारित किए जाते हैं।
2. चरण I: रुचि की अभिव्यक्ति (EoI) का आमंत्रण (नियम 186) - योग्य सलाहकार फर्मों से आवेदन आमंत्रित करने के लिए सार्वजनिक विज्ञापन जारी करना।
3. चरण III: सलाहकारों की संक्षिप्त सूची (शॉर्टलिस्टिंग) बनाना (नियम 187) - प्राप्त आवेदनों की पात्रता का मूल्यांकन करके योग्य फर्मों की एक संक्षिप्त सूची तैयार करना।
4. चरण IV: तकनीकी और वित्तीय बोलियों का मूल्यांकन करना (नियम 188 से 193) - शॉर्टलिस्टेड फर्मों से प्रस्ताव मांगकर तकनीकी और वित्तीय बोलियों का मूल्यांकन करना तथा अनुबंध प्रदान करना।
अतः सही क्रम II -> I -> III -> IV है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) II, I, III, IV

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Procuring consulting services follows a structured sequence. Next, the department issues an invitation for Expression of Interest to identify potential candidates. The authority then shortlists qualified firms, followed by receiving, evaluating, and scoring technical and financial proposals to select the winner.

question_english: Under GFR 2017 and the Compendium of Rules on Advances, advances to government servants are regulated by specific guidelines. Which of the following is classified as an interest-bearing advance?
options_english: Advance of pay on transfer
Personal Computer Advance (PCA)
Leave Travel Concession (LTC) advance
Travelling Allowance (TA) advance on tour
explanation_english:
Under the General Financial Rules (GFR) and the Compendium of Rules on Advances to Government Servants, advances are broadly categorized into two classes:
1. Interest-bearing advances: Advances granted for specific capital assets or welfare purposes where the employee is required to repay the principal amount along with interest calculated at rates prescribed by the Ministry of Finance from time to time. Personal Computer Advance (PCA) and House Building Advance (HBA) are classic examples of interest-bearing advances retained after the 7th Central Pay Commission (7th CPC).
2. Non-interest-bearing advances: Advances granted to facilitate the discharge of official duties or contingent travel requirements. These include Travelling Allowance (TA) advance on tour or transfer, advance of pay on transfer, and Leave Travel Concession (LTC) advance. These carry no interest provided they are adjusted or refunded within the prescribed statutory time limits.
Therefore, Computer Advance is an interest-bearing advance.
explanation_hindi:
सामान्य वित्तीय नियम (GFR) और सरकारी कर्मचारियों को अग्रिम नियमों के संग्रह के अनुसार, सरकारी सेवकों को दिए जाने वाले अग्रिमों को मुख्य रूप से दो श्रेणियों में विभाजित किया गया है:
1. ब्याज सहित अग्रिम (Interest-bearing advances): वे अग्रिम जो विशिष्ट पूंजीगत परिसंपत्तियों या कल्याणकारी उद्देश्यों हेतु दिए जाते हैं, जिनमें कर्मचारी को मूलधन के साथ-साथ वित्त मंत्रालय द्वारा समय-समय पर निर्धारित ब्याज दर का भी भुगतान करना होता है। 7वें केंद्रीय वेतन आयोग (7th CPC) के बाद बरकरार रखे गए 'कंप्यूटर अग्रिम' (Personal Computer Advance) और 'भवन निर्माण अग्रिम' (HBA) इसके प्रमुख उदाहरण हैं।
2. ब्याज मुक्त अग्रिम (Non-interest-bearing advances): सरकारी कर्तव्यों के निष्पादन अथवा यात्रा संबंधी आकस्मिक व्यय हेतु दिए जाने वाले अग्रिम ब्याज मुक्त होते हैं। जैसे- आधिकारिक दौरे या स्थानांतरण पर यात्रा भत्ता (TA) अग्रिम, स्थानांतरण पर वेतन अग्रिम, तथा अवकाश यात्रा रियायत (LTC) अग्रिम। निर्धारित समय-सीमा के भीतर इनका समायोजन या वापसी करने पर कोई ब्याज नहीं लिया जाता है।
अतः, कंप्यूटर अग्रिम एक ब्याज सहित अग्रिम है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (B) Computer Advance

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Advances granted to government employees fall into interest-bearing and non-interest-bearing categories. Computer advance is classified as an interest-bearing advance, requiring repayment of principal followed by interest accrued at government-prescribed interest rates. Conversely, duty-related advances such as travel allowances for official tours, transfer advances, and leave travel concessions are non-interest-bearing personal advances.

question_english: Which of the following statements correctly identifies the regulatory nature of advances granted to government employees for official tours and departmental transfers?
options_english: They carry a heavy compound interest rate equivalent to General Provident Fund (GPF) rates.
They are non-interest-bearing advances meant to meet contingent duty and travel expenses.
They are permanent non-recoverable monetary grants that do not require formal submission of adjustment bills.
They can be sanctioned exclusively by the Department of Expenditure under the Ministry of Finance.
explanation_english:
Under GFR and Supplementary Rules (SR) governing Travelling Allowances, advances sanctioned to government employees for official tours and departmental transfers are strictly non-interest-bearing financial accommodations. The rationale is that an employee proceeding on official duty should not be forced to incur out-of-pocket personal expenditure for public service.
Key regulatory provisions:
1. Tour and transfer advances are provided to meet immediate travel and contingent expenses incurred while performing official duties.
2. Employees are strictly required to settle these advances by submitting detailed adjustment bills accompanied by supporting travel vouchers within prescribed statutory timeframes (15 days for tour TA).
3. If an employee fails to submit adjustment bills in time, penal interest is levied and the unadjusted amount is recovered in a lump sum from the salary.
4. Powers to sanction these routine duty advances are delegated to Heads of Offices and DDOs under the Delegation of Financial Powers Rules (DFPR).
explanation_hindi:
जीएफआर (GFR) और यात्रा भत्ते को विनियमित करने वाले पूरक नियमों (SR) के तहत, आधिकारिक दौरों और विभागीय स्थानांतरण के लिए सरकारी सेवकों को स्वीकृत अग्रिम पूरी तरह से ब्याज मुक्त (non-interest bearing) वित्तीय सुविधाएं हैं। इसका मूल सिद्धांत यह है कि सरकारी कार्य के संपादन हेतु कर्मचारी को अपनी जेब से खर्च करने के लिए विवश नहीं किया जाना चाहिए।

1. दौरा और स्थानांतरण अग्रिम का उद्देश्य आधिकारिक कर्तव्य पालन के दौरान उत्पन्न होने वाले तत्काल यात्रा और आकस्मिक व्यय को पूरा करना है।
2. कर्मचारियों के लिए निर्धारित वैधानिक समय-सीमा (दौरे के लिए 15 दिन) के भीतर सहायक वाउचरों सहित विस्तृत समायोजन बिल प्रस्तुत करके इन अग्रिमों का निपटान करना अनिवार्य होता है।
3. समय पर समायोजन बिल जमा न करने की स्थिति में दंडात्मक ब्याज लगाया जाता है और असमायोजित राशि वेतन से एकमुश्त वसूल कर ली जाती है।
4. वित्तीय शक्तियों के प्रत्यायोजन नियम (DFPR) के तहत कार्यालय प्रमुख (HoO) और आहरण एवं संवितरण अधिकारी (DDO) को ऐसे अग्रिम स्वीकृत करने की शक्तियां प्राप्त हैं।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (B) They are non-interest bearing advances meant to meet contingent duty expenses.
