Under Central Civil Services (Leave Travel Concession) Rules, 1988:
- Statement I is correct: An advance up to 90% of the estimated permissible travel fare may be sanctioned to a government servant for both outward and return journeys.
- Statement II is correct: In case of rail travel, commensurate with the Advance Reservation Period (ARP) of Indian Railways, the advance can be drawn up to 65 days before the proposed date of the outward journey.
- Statement III is correct: The advance must be utilized for the purchase of tickets within the stipulated period (ordinarily within 10 days of drawal). If tickets are not purchased or produced within this timeframe, the entire advance must be refunded immediately in full into the government account.
- Statement IV is incorrect: LTC rules exclusively cover journey transportation fares (rail, authorized air fare, or approved public bus service as per entitlement). Charges for boarding, lodging, hotel stay, tour guides, and local sight-seeing cannot be claimed or paid from the LTC advance.
Therefore, Statements I, II, and III are correct.
explanation_hindi:
केंद्रीय सिविल सेवा (अवकाश यात्रा रियायत) नियमावली, 1988 के अनुसार:
- कथन I सही है: सरकारी सेवक को स्वयं तथा उसके परिवार के पात्र सदस्यों के लिए अनुमानित स्वीकार्य यात्रा किराए का 90% तक अग्रिम स्वीकृत किया जा सकता है।
- कथन II सही है: रेल यात्रा के मामले में, भारतीय रेलवे की अग्रिम आरक्षण अवधि (ARP) के अनुरूप, यात्रा शुरू होने की प्रस्तावित तिथि से 65 दिन पूर्व तक अग्रिम आहरित किया जा सकता है।
- कथन III सही है: अग्रिम प्राप्त करने के बाद यदि निर्धारित समय (सामान्यतः 10 दिन) के भीतर टिकट नहीं खरीदा जाता है, तो अग्रिम की संपूर्ण राशि तुरंत एकमुश्त सरकारी खाते में वापस जमा करनी होती है।
- कथन IV गलत है: एलटीसी अग्रिम केवल यात्रा के परिवहन किराए (पात्रता अनुसार रेल, अधिकृत हवाई यात्रा या अनुमोदित बस किराया) के लिए ही सीमित है। यात्रा के दौरान भोजन (खान-पान), होटल में ठहरने और स्थानीय भ्रमण के खर्चों को एलटीसी अग्रिम से पूरा नहीं किया जा सकता।
अतः कथन I, II और III सही हैं।

question_hindi: एक सरकारी विद्यालय का शिक्षक जो आधिकारिक चुनाव ड्यूटी पर जा रहा है, यात्रा भत्ता (टीए) अग्रिम का अनुरोध करता है। ड्यूटी से लौटने के बाद, शिक्षक छह महीने तक टीए समायोजन बिल प्रस्तुत करने में विफल रहता है। वित्तीय नियमों के अनुसार कार्यालय प्रमुख / प्राचार्य को क्या कार्रवाई करनी चाहिए?

चुनाव ड्यूटी के महत्व को ध्यान में रखते हुए प्रशासनिक देरी को पूरी तरह से माफ कर देना।

कार्यालय प्रमुख के विशेष अनुमोदन से असमायोजित अग्रिम को अधिकृत अनुग्रह भुगतान (ex-gratia) में परिवर्तित करना।

question_english: A government school teacher going on an official election duty tour requests a Travelling Allowance (TA) advance. Upon returning from the tour, the teacher fails to submit the TA adjustment bill for six months. What action should the Head of Office / Principal take as per financial rules?
options_english: Grant another fresh TA advance for the next duty to automatically absorb the previous outstanding balance.
Condone the administrative delay entirely considering that the tour was conducted for official election duty.
Recover the entire outstanding TA advance from the teacher's salary in a lump sum along with penal interest.
Convert the unadjusted advance into an authorized ex-gratia payment with special approval from the Head of Office.
explanation_english:
Under Supplementary Rules (SR) and the Compendium of Rules on Advances:
1. Statutory Time Limit: A government servant who draws a TA advance on tour is required to submit the final adjustment travel claim within 15 days of completing the return journey.
2. Mandatory Recovery: When an employee fails to submit the adjustment bill within the prescribed statutory period, the administrative head / DDO must enforce mandatory financial recovery. The entire outstanding advance amount must be recovered in a single lump sum from the employee's subsequent monthly salary disbursement.
3. Penal Interest: In addition to lump-sum recovery, penal interest (at 2% above the prevailing GPF interest rate) is charged on the unadjusted advance from the date of drawal to the date of recovery.
4. No Discretion: The Head of Office has no administrative power to condone the delay arbitrarily, write off the advance, convert it into an ex-gratia grant, or issue a second advance before the first is settled.
Therefore, the correct action is to recover the entire advance from the salary in a lump sum.
explanation_hindi:
पूरक नियमों (SR) और अग्रिम नियमों के संग्रह के अनुसार:
1. वैधानिक समय-सीमा: आधिकारिक दौरे पर टीए अग्रिम लेने वाले सरकारी सेवक को वापसी यात्रा पूरी होने के 15 दिनों के भीतर अंतिम यात्रा समायोजन बिल प्रस्तुत करना अनिवार्य होता है।
2. अनिवार्य वसूली: जब कोई कर्मचारी निर्धारित समय-सीमा के भीतर यात्रा भत्ता समायोजन बिल प्रस्तुत करने में विफल रहता है, तो प्रशासनिक प्रमुख / डीडीओ को अनिवार्य वित्तीय वसूली करनी होती है। पूरी बकाया अग्रिम राशि कर्मचारी के आगामी वेतन से एकमुश्त वसूल की जानी चाहिए।
3. दंडात्मक ब्याज: एकमुश्त वसूली के अलावा, आहरण की तारीख से वसूली की तारीख तक असमायोजित अग्रिम पर दंडात्मक ब्याज (GPF दर से 2% अधिक) भी लगाया जाता है।
4. कोई विवेकाधिकार नहीं: कार्यालय प्रमुख के पास मनमाने ढंग से देरी को माफ करने, इसे बट्टे खाते में डालने, इसे अनुग्रह अनुदान (ex-gratia) में बदलने या पिछला अग्रिम चुकता किए बिना दूसरा अग्रिम जारी करने का कोई अधिकार नहीं है।
अतः सही कार्रवाई शिक्षक के वेतन से पूरी बकाया राशि की एकमुश्त वसूली करना है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (C) Recover the entire outstanding TA advance from the teacher's salary in a lump sum.

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: from the teacher's salary in a lump sum. When an employee fails to submit a travel allowance adjustment bill within the stipulated statutory period following tour completion, the administrative head must enforce financial recovery. The entire outstanding advance amount must be recovered in a single lump sum from the employee's subsequent salary payment, alongside penal interest if mandated under financial rules.

question_hindi:
नीचे दो कथन दिए गए हैं: एक को अभिकथन (A) और दूसरे को कारण (R) के रूप में लेबल किया गया है।
अभिकथन (A): किसी सरकारी सेवक को यात्रा भत्ता (TA) का दूसरा अग्रिम सामान्यतः तब तक नहीं दिया जाना चाहिए जब तक कि पहले अग्रिम का हिसाब प्रस्तुत और समायोजित न कर दिया गया हो।
कारण (R): अग्रिमों का तत्काल और समयबद्ध समायोजन व्यक्तियों के हाथों में सरकारी धन के अनधिकृत संचय को रोकने तथा सार्वजनिक धन के गबन को रोकने के लिए अनिवार्य है।
उपर्युक्त कथनों के आलोक में, नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सही उत्तर का चयन कीजिए:

(A) और (R) दोनों सही हैं, लेकिन (R), (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं है

subject: UPSC Principal Paper
question_english:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).
Assertion (A): A second advance for Travelling Allowance (TA) should not normally be granted to a government servant until an account has been rendered and adjusted for the first advance.
Reason (R): Immediate and timely adjustment of advances is essential to prevent unauthorized accumulation of public money in the hands of individuals and to prevent misappropriation.
In light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options_english: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is true but (R) is false
(A) is false but (R) is true
explanation_english:
Under Rule 291 of GFR 2017 and general principles of government financial accounting:
- Assertion (A) is true: Financial rules explicitly dictate that no second advance for travel or other official purposes should normally be granted to an employee while a previous advance remains outstanding and unadjusted. Sanctioning overlapping advances without settlement of prior accounts is a grave procedural irregularity.
- Reason (R) is true: The foundational rationale for this restriction is financial prudence and internal audit control. Allowing advances to remain unadjusted results in unauthorized retention and accumulation of government cash in private hands, increasing the risk of loss, cash hoarding, and fraudulent misappropriation of public funds.
Moreover, Reason (R) provides the exact logical and regulatory justification for why Assertion (A) is strictly enforced.
Therefore, both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
explanation_hindi:
जीएफआर 2017 के नियम 291 तथा सरकारी वित्तीय लेखांकन के सामान्य सिद्धांतों के अनुसार:
- अभिकथन (A) सही है: वित्तीय नियमों में यह स्पष्ट रूप से निर्धारित है कि किसी भी कर्मचारी को यात्रा या अन्य आधिकारिक उद्देश्यों हेतु दूसरा अग्रिम तब तक स्वीकृत नहीं किया जाना चाहिए जब तक कि पहले अग्रिम का पूर्ण हिसाब प्रस्तुत और समायोजित न कर दिया गया हो। पिछले खातों के निपटारे के बिना नया अग्रिम देना गंभीर प्रक्रियात्मक अनियमितता है।
- कारण (R) सही है: इस प्रतिबंध का मूल आधार वित्तीय सतर्कता और आंतरिक लेखापरीक्षा नियंत्रण है। अग्रिमों को असमायोजित छोड़ने से व्यक्तियों के हाथों में सरकारी धन का अनधिकृत संचय और प्रतिधारण होता है, जिससे वित्तीय लापरवाही, धन के अनुचित उपयोग और सार्वजनिक धन के गबन का जोखिम काफी बढ़ जाता है।
इसके अतिरिक्त, कारण (R) सीधे तौर पर यह सिद्ध करता है कि अभिकथन (A) को एक सख्त वित्तीय नियंत्रण के रूप में क्यों लागू किया गया है।
अतः (A) और (R) दोनों सही हैं और (R), (A) की सही व्याख्या है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: correct explanation of (A) Financial rules dictate that a second travel advance should not be sanctioned to an employee until the previous advance has been fully accounted for or adjusted. Timely settlement prevents the improper accumulation of public funds in individual hands, ensures accurate accounting, and mitigates risks of financial negligence, unauthorized retention, or potential misappropriation of government funds.

question_english: Under the Supplementary Rules and central accounting guidelines, what is the stipulated time limit for a government employee to submit the adjustment bill for a TA advance taken for an official tour, following the completion of the return journey?
options_english: 30 days
60 days
15 days
90 days
explanation_english:
Under Supplementary Rules (SR) and the Compendium of Rules on Advances:
1. Prescribed Time Limit: A government employee who draws a travel allowance advance for an official tour is statutorily required to submit the final adjustment travel claim within 15 days of completing the return journey.
2. Important Distinction: For travel where NO advance is drawn, the Department of Expenditure (OM dated 13.03.2018) revised the submission time limit for regular TA claims to 60 days. However, when a TA advance has been drawn from the public exchequer, the strict time limit for submission of the adjustment bill remains 15 days.
3. Consequence of Non-Compliance: Failure to submit the adjustment bill within 15 days leads to recovery of the entire advance in a lump sum from the employee's monthly pay, together with penal interest at 2% above the GPF rate from the date of drawal.
Therefore, the stipulated time limit is 15 days.
explanation_hindi:
पूरक नियमों (SR) और अग्रिम नियमों के संग्रह के अनुसार:
1. निर्धारित समय-सीमा: आधिकारिक दौरे के लिए यात्रा भत्ता (TA) अग्रिम लेने वाले सरकारी कर्मचारी के लिए वापसी यात्रा पूर्ण होने के 15 दिनों के भीतर अंतिम यात्रा समायोजन दावा प्रस्तुत करना वैधानिक रूप से अनिवार्य है।
2. महत्वपूर्ण अंतर: उन मामलों में जहाँ कोई अग्रिम नहीं लिया गया है, व्यय विभाग के 13.03.2018 के कार्यालय ज्ञापन द्वारा नियमित टीए दावों की प्रस्तुति की समय-सीमा 60 दिन निर्धारित की गई है। परंतु जहाँ सरकारी खजाने से टीए अग्रिम आहरित किया गया है, वहाँ समायोजन बिल प्रस्तुत करने की सख्त समय-सीमा केवल 15 दिन ही है।
3. गैर-अनुपालन का परिणाम: 15 दिनों के भीतर समायोजन बिल प्रस्तुत न करने पर आहरण की तारीख से GPF दर से 2% अधिक दंडात्मक ब्याज सहित कर्मचारी के मासिक वेतन से पूरे अग्रिम की एकमुश्त वसूली की जाती है।
अतः निर्धारित समय-सीमा 15 दिन है।

question_english: Which of the following advances was abolished for Central Government employees as a permanent standing provision following the implementation of the 7th Central Pay Commission recommendations?
options_english: Personal Computer Advance
Festival Advance
Travelling Allowance (TA) Advance on Tour
Leave Travel Concession (LTC) Advance
explanation_english:
Following the acceptance of the recommendations of the 7th Central Pay Commission (7th CPC) by the Government of India (Department of Expenditure OM No. 12(1)/E.II(A)/2016 dated October 7, 2016):
1. Abolished Advances: Numerous minor interest-free and interest-bearing advances were abolished to rationalize accounting procedures and eliminate unnecessary paperwork. These abolished advances included Festival Advance, Natural Calamity Advance, Warm Clothing Advance, Advance of Pay on Transfer, and Bicycle Advance.
2. Retained Advances: Only three categories of advances were retained:
   - House Building Advance (HBA) - Interest-bearing
   - Personal Computer Advance (PCA) - Interest-bearing
   - Operational duty advances such as TA/DA advance on tour/transfer, LTC advance, and medical advance.
(Note: While temporary interest-free schemes like the Special Festival Advance Scheme were intermittently launched as economic relief packages via prepaid RuPay cards during the pandemic, Festival Advance was formally abolished as a regular standing rule).
Therefore, Festival Advance was abolished.

question_english: Under the provisions of General Financial Rules (GFR) and rules regulating government advances, in which of the following circumstances is an advance of pay strictly NOT permitted?
options_english: On transfer of an employee to a new station in the public interest.
As immediate relief to the family of a government servant who dies while in service.
On proceeding on a prolonged official tour of duty.
For meeting personal household groceries and domestic living costs at the end of the month.
explanation_english:
Under the Compendium of Rules on Advances and GFR 2017:
1. Authorized Circumstances for Pay Advances: Advances of pay or immediate financial assistance are permissible strictly under statutory conditions, such as:
   - On transfer to another station (historically permitted before 7th CPC revisions to assist in initial family relocation).
   - Immediate relief to the family of a government servant who dies while in service (under Rule 79 of the Compendium of Rules on Advances, providing urgent subsistence relief pending final settlement of terminal benefits).
   - Proceeding on a prolonged tour of official duty away from headquarters.
2. Prohibited Uses: Granting advances of pay to meet private, domestic living expenses, monthly groceries, or personal financial shortfalls is completely unauthorized and strictly prohibited. Utilizing public money for such personal purposes violates Rule 21 of GFR 2017 (Standards of Financial Propriety) and amounts to unauthorized diversion of government funds.
Therefore, Option D is strictly NOT permitted.

question_english: What is the meaning and purpose of a "Permanent Advance" or "Imprest" in the context of government offices and schools?
options_english: A fixed sum placed at the disposal of an officer to meet urgent and petty contingent expenditures before funds can be drawn on regular bills.
A permanent administrative increment granted in the basic pay scale of a government employee.
A long-term interest-bearing loan sanctioned to an employee for constructing a permanent residential house.
An emergency cash relief fund sanctioned directly by the Prime Minister for disaster response.
explanation_english:
Under Rule 322 of General Financial Rules (GFR), 2017 and Central Government Account (Receipts and Payments) Rules:
1. Definition: A permanent advance, universally termed an "Imprest", is a fixed sum of money placed at the disposal of an administrative officer (such as a Head of Office, Drawing and Disbursing Officer, or School Principal) to enable immediate payment for routine, small-value contingent office expenses before funds can be drawn on regular contingent bills from the Pay and Accounts Office (PAO).
2. Administrative Utility: In the day-to-day administration of an office or educational institution, numerous small expenses arise (e.g., postage, urgent minor repairs, cartage, emergency stationery). Presenting individual bills to the PAO for each petty transaction would cause severe delays and operational paralysis. The imprest system provides the operational flexibility needed to settle petty charges immediately.
3. Continuous Replenishment: As petty payments are made from the imprest, paid vouchers are accumulated and submitted via an imprest recoupment bill to reimburse and restore the cash balance to its original sanctioned limit.
Therefore, Option A correctly defines an imprest.
explanation_hindi:
सामान्य वित्तीय नियम (GFR) 2017 के नियम 322 और केंद्रीय सरकारी लेखा (प्राप्ति और भुगतान) नियमों के अनुसार:
1. परिभाषा: स्थायी अग्रिम, जिसे सामान्यतः "इम्प्रेस्ट" (Imprest) कहा जाता है, किसी प्रशासनिक अधिकारी (जैसे कार्यालय प्रमुख, आहरण एवं संवितरण अधिकारी / DDO या विद्यालय प्राचार्य) के अधीन रखी गई धन की एक निश्चित राशि होती है, ताकि वेतन एवं लेखा कार्यालय (PAO) से नियमित आकस्मिक बिलों पर धन प्राप्त होने की प्रतीक्षा किए बिना दिन-प्रतिदिन के छोटे-मोटे आकस्मिक खर्चों का तत्काल भुगतान किया जा सके।
2. प्रशासनिक उपयोगिता: किसी कार्यालय या शिक्षण संस्थान के दैनिक प्रशासन में कई छोटे खर्च सामने आते हैं (जैसे डाक खर्च, छोटी आकस्मिक मरम्मत, स्थानीय ढुलाई, तात्कालिक स्टेशनरी आदि)। प्रत्येक छोटे लेनदेन के लिए पीएओ में अलग-अलग बिल भेजना भारी देरी और प्रशासनिक कार्यों में बाधा उत्पन्न करेगा। इम्प्रेस्ट प्रणाली इन छोटे भुगतानों को तुरंत निपटाने की सुविधा प्रदान करती है।
3. निरंतर प्रतिपूर्ति: इम्प्रेस्ट से भुगतान किए जाने के बाद, भुगतान किए गए वाउचरों को एकत्र कर एक प्रतिपूर्ति बिल (Recoupment Bill) के माध्यम से प्रस्तुत किया जाता है जिससे नकद शेष राशि वापस मूल स्वीकृत सीमा तक पहुँच जाती है।
अतः विकल्प A सही परिभाषा प्रस्तुत करता है।

question_english:
Consider the following statements regarding the Imprest (Permanent Advance) System:
I. The quantum of permanent advance is fixed by the competent authority based on the routine petty cash requirements of the office.
II. The imprest cash should be kept strictly separate and not mixed up with any other government or private cash held by the officer.
III. The imprest cannot be recouped during the year and must last for the entire financial year without replenishment.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
options_english: I and II only
II and III only
I and III only
I, II and III
explanation_english:
Under Rule 322 of GFR 2017 and Government Accounting Rules:
- Statement I is correct: The amount of the permanent advance is fixed by the Head of Department or designated competent authority based on a realistic assessment of the minimum essential petty cash requirements necessary for efficient day-to-day office operations, normally not exceeding the monthly petty expenditure.
- Statement II is correct: Under Receipt and Payment Rules, imprest cash is a distinct custody fund and must never be commingled with regular government revenues, departmental chest receipts, undisbursed pay and allowances, or personal private cash. It must be accounted for independently in a dedicated Imprest Cash Register.
- Statement III is incorrect: The defining operational characteristic of the imprest system is periodic recoupment. Whenever the petty cash balance is depleted (or at regular monthly/fortnightly intervals), the holding officer submits an imprest recoupment bill accompanied by paid sub-vouchers to the accounts office. Upon audit and payment, the exact expended amount is reimbursed, constantly restoring the cash balance to its original sanctioned limit. It does not have to last the entire year without replenishment.
Therefore, Statements I and II only are correct.
explanation_hindi:
जीएफआर 2017 के नियम 322 और सरकारी लेखा नियमों के अनुसार:
- कथन I सही है: स्थायी अग्रिम की राशि विभागाध्यक्ष या नामित सक्षम प्राधिकारी द्वारा कार्यालय के दैनिक कार्यों के कुशल संचालन हेतु आवश्यक न्यूनतम खुदरा नकद आवश्यकताओं के वास्तविक आकलन के आधार पर तय की जाती है, जो सामान्यतः एक महीने के खुदरा खर्च से अधिक नहीं होती।
- कथन II सही है: प्राप्ति और भुगतान नियमों के तहत, इम्प्रेस्ट नकदी एक विशिष्ट अभिरक्षा निधि है और इसे नियमित सरकारी राजस्व, विभागीय चेस्ट प्राप्तियों, अवितरित वेतन और भत्तों, या व्यक्तिगत नकदी के साथ कभी नहीं मिलाया जाना चाहिए। इसका हिसाब एक समर्पित 'इम्प्रेस्ट रोकड़ बही' (Imprest Cash Book) में स्वतंत्र रूप से रखा जाना अनिवार्य है।
- कथन III गलत है: इम्प्रेस्ट प्रणाली की सबसे प्रमुख विशेषता इसकी समय-समय पर प्रतिपूर्ति (Recoupment) है। जैसे ही खुदरा नकदी कम होती है (या नियमित मासिक/पाक्षिक अंतराल पर), प्रभारी अधिकारी भुगतान किए गए उप-वाउचरों के साथ एक प्रतिपूर्ति बिल लेखा कार्यालय को प्रस्तुत करता है। सत्यापन और भुगतान के पश्चात खर्च की गई सटीक राशि वापस मिल जाती है, जिससे नकद शेष निरंतर अपनी मूल स्वीकृत सीमा पर बना रहता है। ऐसा नहीं है कि इसे बिना प्रतिपूर्ति के पूरे साल चलाना पड़े।
अतः केवल कथन I और II सही हैं।

question_english: A school Principal holds a sanctioned permanent advance (imprest) of Rs. 5,000. During a month, the Principal incurs legitimate office expenditures totaling Rs. 4,500 on urgent postal dispatches, minor plumbing repairs, and laboratory cartage. What is the correct procedural action the Principal must take next?
options_english: Submit an imprest recoupment bill along with verified sub-vouchers for Rs. 4,500 to the accounts officer to restore the cash balance.
Close the permanent advance account immediately and suspend all petty contingent expenditures until the next financial year.
Deduct Rs. 4,500 proportionately from the monthly salaries of subordinate office staff to replenish the fund.
Request the School Management Committee (SMC) members to collect voluntary cash donations of Rs. 4,500 from parents.
explanation_english:
Under Rule 322 of GFR 2017 and Government Accounting Rules:
1. Operating Mechanism of Permanent Advance: The permanent advance operates as a revolving imprest. The sum of physical cash in the office safe plus unrecouped paid sub-vouchers must at all times equal the total sanctioned advance limit:
   Sanctioned Advance (Rs. 5,000) = Cash Balance (Rs. 500) + Paid Sub-vouchers (Rs. 4,500).
2. Recoupment Process: To restore the liquid cash balance back to Rs. 5,000, the Principal / Head of Office prepares an Imprest Recoupment Bill on the standard contingent bill format, attaches the original stamped sub-vouchers duly cancelled with "Paid and Cancelled", certifies the payments, and submits it to the Pay and Accounts Office (PAO).
3. Re-crediting: Upon audit and sanction, the accounts officer issues a cheque / electronic credit for Rs. 4,500, replenishing the school's petty cash balance back to Rs. 5,000.
4. Prohibited actions: Freezing administrative functions, deducting from staff salaries, or seeking private donations are illegal, unethical, and represent gross violations of financial rules.
Therefore, Option A is the correct procedural action.
explanation_hindi:
जीएफआर 2017 के नियम 322 और सरकारी लेखा नियमों के अनुसार:
1. स्थायी अग्रिम की कार्यप्रणाली: स्थायी अग्रिम एक परिक्रामी इम्प्रेस्ट के रूप में संचालित होता है। कार्यालय की तिजोरी में उपलब्ध भौतिक नकदी और प्रतिपूर्ति हेतु लंबित भुगतान किए गए उप-वाउचरों का योग हमेशा कुल स्वीकृत अग्रिम सीमा के बराबर होना चाहिए:
   स्वीकृत अग्रिम (₹5,000) = नकद शेष (₹500) + भुगतान किए गए उप-वाउचर (₹4,500)।
2. प्रतिपूर्ति प्रक्रिया (Recoupment): नकद शेष को पुनः ₹5,000 तक लाने के लिए, प्राचार्य/कार्यालय प्रमुख मानक आकस्मिक बिल प्रारूप पर एक 'इम्प्रेस्ट प्रतिपूर्ति बिल' तैयार करते हैं, "भुगतान किया गया और रद्द किया गया" (Paid and Cancelled) मोहर लगे मूल उप-वाउचर संलग्न करते हैं, खर्च को प्रमाणित करते हैं और इसे वेतन एवं लेखा कार्यालय (PAO) को प्रस्तुत करते हैं।
3. पुनर्भरण: लेखा परीक्षा और पास आदेश के बाद, लेखा अधिकारी ₹4,500 का इलेक्ट्रॉनिक भुगतान जारी करता है, जिससे विद्यालय की खुदरा नकदी वापस पूरी ₹5,000 हो जाती है।
4. प्रतिबंधित कार्य: प्रशासनिक कार्यों को रोकना, कर्मचारियों के वेतन से कटौती करना, या निजी दान मांगना पूर्णतः अवैध और वित्तीय नियमों का गंभीर उल्लंघन है।
अतः विकल्प A सही प्रक्रियात्मक कार्रवाई है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) Submit an imprest recoupment bill with vouchers for Rs. 4,500 to restore balance.

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: vouchers for Rs. 4,500 to restore balance. When expenses are paid from an office permanent advance, the holding officer must periodically submit an imprest recoupment bill accompanied by sub-vouchers to the accounts officer. Upon audit and verification, the exact spent amount is reimbursed, restoring the cash imprest balance to its original sanctioned limit for ongoing petty administrative expenditure.

question_hindi:

अभिकथन (A): किसी अधिकारी के पास रखे गए स्थायी अग्रिम की पावती (Acknowledgment) प्रतिवर्ष 1 अप्रैल को लेखा अधिकारी को भेजी जानी अनिवार्य है।

उपर्युक्त कथनों के आलोक में, नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सही उत्तर का चयन कीजिए:

question_english:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).
Assertion (A): The permanent advance held by an officer must be acknowledged by them to the Accounts Officer on the first of April every year.
Reason (R): This annual acknowledgment verifies the physical existence and correctness of the advance at the beginning of each financial year, ensuring accounting accountability.
In light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options_english: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is true but (R) is false
(A) is false but (R) is true
explanation_english:
Under Rule 322(3) of GFR 2017 and Central Government Account (Receipts and Payments) Rules:
- Assertion (A) is true: Every administrative officer who holds a permanent advance (imprest) is required under statutory rules to formally send an acknowledgment of the exact amount of the advance held by them to the Accounts Officer on the 1st of April each financial year (as well as whenever there is a transfer of administrative charge).
- Reason (R) is true: An imprest involves public funds kept permanently outside the treasury chest under the immediate physical custody of the DDO. Annual acknowledgment acts as a primary audit verification tool to ensure that the physical cash plus valid unrecouped vouchers equal the total sanctioned advance at the opening of the fiscal year, preventing unrecorded deficits, embezzlement, or unauthorized retention.
Reason (R) provides the exact regulatory objective and direct explanation for why Assertion (A) is mandated.
Therefore, both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
explanation_hindi:
जीएफआर 2017 के नियम 322(3) और केंद्रीय सरकारी लेखा (प्राप्ति और भुगतान) नियमों के अनुसार:
- अभिकथन (A) सही है: स्थायी अग्रिम (इम्प्रेस्ट) रखने वाले प्रत्येक प्रशासनिक अधिकारी के लिए यह वैधानिक अनिवार्यता है कि वह प्रत्येक वित्तीय वर्ष की 1 अप्रैल को (तथा प्रशासनिक प्रभार के हस्तांतरण के समय भी) अपने पास मौजूद अग्रिम की सटीक राशि की औपचारिक पावती (Acknowledgment) लेखा अधिकारी को प्रेषित करे।
- कारण (R) सही है: इम्प्रेस्ट के अंतर्गत सरकारी खजाने से बाहर डीडीओ की अभिरक्षा में स्थायी नकदी रखी जाती है। वार्षिक पावती एक प्रमुख लेखापरीक्षा सत्यापन साधन के रूप में कार्य करती है, जो यह सुनिश्चित करती है कि नए वित्तीय वर्ष की शुरुआत में भौतिक नकदी और वैध गैर-प्रतिपूरित वाउचरों का योग कुल स्वीकृत अग्रिम के बराबर है, जिससे किसी भी अनधिकृत कमी, गबन या धन के अनुचित उपयोग को रोका जा सके।
कारण (R) सीधे तौर पर यह स्पष्ट करता है कि अभिकथन (A) की अनिवार्यता क्यों तय की गई है।
अतः (A) और (R) दोनों सही हैं और (R), (A) की सही व्याख्या है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: correct explanation of (A) Officers holding permanent advances are required to formally acknowledge holding the funds on the first day of April each financial year. This annual acknowledgment verifies the physical availability and correctness of cash balances at the start of the year, maintaining accounting accountability and ensuring continuous monitoring of delegated petty cash balances.

question_english: Which of the following statements correctly identifies the statutory scope and regulatory limitations of an office Permanent Advance (Imprest)?
options_english: It can be freely utilized by the Head of Office to disburse regular monthly salaries and wages of Group 'D' casual staff.
It is strictly intended for meeting petty contingent charges that require immediate settlement before regular funds can be drawn from the accounts office.
It can be validly utilized to grant temporary cash advances to subordinate staff members for urgent personal medical needs.
The total imprest amount can be indefinitely enhanced by the Head of Office at their own administrative discretion.
explanation_english:
Under Rule 322 of GFR 2017:
1. Statutory Purpose: An office permanent advance is strictly and exclusively intended for meeting petty contingent charges that require immediate settlement before funds can be obtained on a regular contingent bill from the Pay and Accounts Office (PAO).
2. Prohibited Uses: Imprest funds can NEVER be utilized for:
   - Paying regular monthly salaries, wages, or honoraria to permanent or casual staff.
   - Extending personal loans, temporary borrowings, or financial assistance to employees, peons, or officers under any circumstances.
   - Circumventing standard public procurement procedures or making split purchases to evade tender limits.
3. Sanctioning Limit: A Head of Office cannot enhance the imprest amount unilaterally; only the Head of Department (HoD) or designated Competent Authority under DFPR can revise or enhance the sanctioned imprest limit after evaluating administrative necessity.
Therefore, Option B is the correct statement.
explanation_hindi:
जीएफआर 2017 के नियम 322 के तहत:
1. वैधानिक उद्देश्य: कार्यालय स्थायी अग्रिम का उद्देश्य केवल और केवल उन छोटे आकस्मिक व्ययों (Petty Contingent Charges) को पूरा करना है जिनका भुगतान वेतन एवं लेखा कार्यालय (PAO) से नियमित आकस्मिक बिल पर धन प्राप्त होने की प्रतीक्षा किए बिना तत्काल किया जाना अनिवार्य होता है।
2. प्रतिबंधित उपयोग: इम्प्रेस्ट निधि का उपयोग निम्नलिखित कार्यों के लिए कभी नहीं किया जा सकता:
   - नियमित या आकस्मिक कर्मचारियों के मासिक वेतन, मजदूरी या मानदेय का भुगतान करना।
   - किसी भी परिस्थिति में कर्मचारियों, चपरासियों या अधिकारियों को व्यक्तिगत ऋण, अस्थायी उधार या वित्तीय सहायता देना।
   - मानक सार्वजनिक खरीद प्रक्रियाओं को दरकिनार करना या निविदा सीमाओं से बचने के लिए खरीद को टुकड़ों में विभाजित करना।
3. सीमा निर्धारण: कार्यालय प्रमुख एकतरफा रूप से इम्प्रेस्ट की राशि में वृद्धि नहीं कर सकता; केवल डीएफपीआर (DFPR) के तहत सक्षम प्राधिकारी/विभागाध्यक्ष ही प्रशासनिक आवश्यकता के मूल्यांकन के बाद स्वीकृत सीमा को बढ़ा सकते हैं।
अतः विकल्प B सही कथन है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (B) It is strictly intended for petty contingent charges requiring payment before drawing funds from PAO.

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: charges requiring payment before drawing funds from PAO. An office permanent advance is strictly intended for paying petty contingent charges that require immediate settlement before regular funds can be drawn from the accounts office. Imprest cash cannot be utilized for disbursing regular staff salaries, personal staff loans, or unauthorized personal advances, nor can its limit be enhanced without higher competent authority sanction.

question_english: As an educational administrator or Drawing and Disbursing Officer (DDO), which of the following disbursements should NEVER be made from the office imprest account under financial rules?
options_english: Paying speed post and registered mail dispatch charges for urgent official examination documents.
Paying a plumber Rs. 500 for emergency fixing of a leaking tap in the school staff room.
Purchasing an emergency padlock and duplicate keys for the school examination strong room for Rs. 200.
Disbursing a personal monetary loan of Rs. 2,000 to a peon to meet domestic family obligations.
explanation_english:
Under Rule 21 (Standards of Financial Propriety) and Rule 322 of GFR 2017:
1. Permissible Payments from Imprest: Legitimate small office contingent expenses that cannot wait for regular treasury billing are fully permissible. Examples include emergency plumbing repairs, dispatch of urgent official letters via speed post, and essential minor hardware (such as locks and keys for securing office records).
2. Prohibited Payments: Utilizing public imprest cash to grant private monetary loans or financial advances to employees—no matter how urgent or compassionate their domestic circumstances may be—is an absolute violation of financial discipline. In government financial accounting, using public funds for personal accommodation constitutes temporary misappropriation (defalcation) of public money, attracting major penalty proceedings under CCS (CCA) Rules.
Therefore, disbursing a personal loan of Rs. 2,000 to a peon should NEVER be made from the imprest account.
explanation_hindi:
जीएफआर 2017 के नियम 21 (वित्तीय औचित्य के मानक) और नियम 322 के अनुसार:
1. इम्प्रेस्ट से अनुमत भुगतान: कार्यालय के वैध छोटे आकस्मिक खर्च जिन्हें नियमित बिलिंग तक नहीं टाला जा सकता, पूरी तरह से अनुमत हैं। जैसे- आपातकालीन नलसाजी मरम्मत, स्पीड पोस्ट द्वारा जरूरी डाक प्रेषण, तथा कार्यालय रिकॉर्ड की सुरक्षा हेतु ताला-चाबी खरीदना।
2. निषिद्ध भुगतान: कर्मचारियों को व्यक्तिगत नकद ऋण या अग्रिम देने के लिए सरकारी इम्प्रेस्ट नकदी का उपयोग करना—चाहे उनकी घरेलू परिस्थितियां कितनी भी गंभीर या सहानुभूतिपूर्ण क्यों न हों—वित्तीय अनुशासन का पूर्ण उल्लंघन है। सरकारी लेखांकन में निजी सहायता हेतु सार्वजनिक धन का उपयोग करना 'सरकारी धन का अस्थायी गबन' (misappropriation) माना जाता है, जिसके लिए सीसीएस (सीसीए) नियमों के तहत बड़ी शास्ति की अनुशासनात्मक कार्रवाई की जा सकती है।
अतः चपरासी को ₹2,000 का व्यक्तिगत ऋण इम्प्रेस्ट से कभी भी नहीं दिया जाना चाहिए।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (D) Disbursing a personal loan of Rs. 2,000 to a peon.

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: a peon. Office imprest funds are strictly reserved for official petty contingent expenses such as emergency repairs, postage, and essential minor office supplies. Utilizing permanent advance cash to disburse personal monetary loans to employees constitutes a grave financial irregularity and a clear misappropriation of public funds, regardless of the employee's urgency.

question_hindi: वित्तीय शक्तियों के प्रत्यायोजन नियम (DFPR) और सामान्य वित्तीय नियम (GFR) के अंतर्गत, किसी अधीनस्थ कार्यालय या विद्यालय के लिए स्थायी अग्रिम (इम्प्रेस्ट) स्वीकृत करने का अधिकार किसे प्राप्त है?

question_english: Under the Delegation of Financial Powers Rules (DFPR) and General Financial Rules (GFR), who is empowered to sanction a Permanent Advance (Imprest) for a subordinate office or school?
options_english: The Senior Cashier or Accounts Assistant maintaining the cash book of the subordinate office.
The Senior Branch Manager of the local public sector bank handling the departmental account.
The Chief Minister of the State acting through the Department of Finance cabinet committee.
The Head of Department (HoD) / Competent Authority as designated under DFPR.
explanation_english:
Under Rule 322 of GFR 2017 read in conjunction with Schedule V of the Delegation of Financial Powers Rules (DFPR):
1. Sanctioning Authority: The Head of Department (HoD) or an authority specifically designated as a Competent Authority under DFPR possesses the statutory power to create and sanction a permanent advance (imprest) for subordinate offices and institutions under their administrative control.
2. Assessment Criteria: The sanctioning authority fixes the quantum of the permanent advance based on a careful assessment of the minimum essential petty cash requirements necessary for efficient day-to-day office operations, in consultation with the accredited financial adviser / accounts authority.
3. Institutional Custodians: Subordinate office cashiers, bank branch managers, or political executives outside the statutory financial delegation hierarchy have no legal authority to determine or sanction government imprest advances.
Therefore, the Head of Department / Competent Authority as per DFPR holds the authority.
explanation_hindi:

2. मूल्यांकन के मानदंड: सक्षम प्राधिकारी मान्यता प्राप्त वित्तीय सलाहकार/लेखा प्राधिकारी के परामर्श से कार्यालय के कुशल दैनिक संचालन के लिए आवश्यक न्यूनतम खुदरा नकद आवश्यकताओं के सावधानीपूर्वक मूल्यांकन के आधार पर स्थायी अग्रिम की सीमा तय करता है।
3. संस्थागत सीमाएं: अधीनस्थ कार्यालय के कैशियर, बैंक शाखा प्रबंधक या वित्तीय प्रत्यायोजन पदानुक्रम से बाहर के राजनीतिक पदाधिकारियों को सरकारी इम्प्रेस्ट अग्रिम निर्धारित करने या स्वीकृत करने का कोई कानूनी अधिकार नहीं है।
अतः सही उत्तर डीएफपीआर के तहत विभागाध्यक्ष / सक्षम प्राधिकारी है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (D) The Head of Department / Competent Authority as per DFPR.

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Authority as per DFPR. Sanctioning a permanent advance for an establishment falls under the administrative authority of the Head of Department or designated competent authority under Delegation of Financial Powers Rules. The sanctioning authority fixes the imprest limit after assessing the minimum essential petty cash requirements necessary for efficient day-to-day office operations.

question_english: At the close of the financial year on 31st March, how should the outstanding unspent balance in the permanent advance (imprest) register be accounted for if the establishment is closing the imprest account?
options_english: The unspent balance must be formally refunded and deposited into the Government Account.
It should be disbursed as a performance bonus among office staff members.
It should be transferred to the local Vidyalaya Kalyan Samiti (VKS) bank account.
It can be retained and carried forward as personal cash by the Head of Office.
explanation_english: Under Rule 322 of the General Financial Rules (GFR), 2017 read with Rule 90 to 95 of the Central Government Account (Receipts and Payments) Rules, 1983, a permanent advance (imprest) is granted to a Head of Office (HOO) or Drawing and Disbursing Officer (DDO) to meet emergent, unforeseen, and petty contingent expenditures before drawing funds on regular bills. At the end of the financial year (31st March), if an office is closing its permanent advance or when directed by treasury/accounts authorities, all vouchers for expenditure incurred up to that date must be adjusted, and the remaining unspent physical cash balance must be formally refunded into the Consolidated Fund of India / Government Account via a military/civil treasury challan. Government financial discipline strictly prohibits retaining public money as private or personal cash, distributing public funds as unapproved staff bonuses, or irregularly diverting imprest money into non-governmental, local school management (e.g., VKS/SMC), or commercial bank accounts.
explanation_hindi: सामान्य वित्तीय नियम (GFR), 2017 के नियम 322 तथा केंद्रीय सरकार खाता (प्राप्ति एवं भुगतान) नियम, 1983 के नियम 90 से 95 के अनुसार, कार्यालय प्रमुख (HOO) या आहरण एवं संवितरण अधिकारी (DDO) को नियमित बिलों पर धनराशि आहरित करने से पूर्व आकस्मिक एवं तत्काल छोटे खर्चों को पूरा करने हेतु स्थायी अग्रिम (इम्प्रेस्ट) स्वीकृत किया जाता है। वित्तीय वर्ष की समाप्ति (31 मार्च) पर यदि कार्यालय द्वारा स्थायी अग्रिम को बंद किया जा रहा है या लेखा नियमों के तहत वर्ष के अंत में समायोजन अपेक्षित है, तो उस तिथि तक किए गए व्यय के सभी वाउचरों का विधिवत समायोजन किया जाना चाहिए तथा बची हुई अप्रयुक्त नकद राशि को चालान के माध्यम से सरकारी खाते (राजकोष) में अनिवार्य रूप से वापस जमा किया जाना चाहिए। वित्तीय नियमों के तहत सरकारी धनराशि को निजी नकदी के रूप में रखने, कर्मचारियों में बोनस के रूप में बांटने अथवा विद्यालय प्रबंधन/कल्याण समिति (VKS/SMC) जैसे स्थानीय बैंक खातों में अवैध रूप से अंतरित करने की सख्त मनाही है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) The unspent balance should be refunded to the Government Account.

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: the Government Account. When an establishment closes its permanent advance or when required by specific accounting directions at year-end closure, any unspent cash balance must be formally refunded into the government account. Imprest funds cannot be retained as personal cash, disbursed as bonuses, or illegally transferred into non-governmental or local committee accounts.

question_english: According to the store accounting framework laid down in GFR 2017, how are government assets and stores broadly categorized for the maintenance of stock registers?
options_english: Financial accounting assets and Social infrastructure assets
Fixed assets, Consumable stores, and Non-consumable stores
Liquid monetary assets and Frozen capital assets
Proprietary commercial assets and Leased statutory assets
explanation_english: Rule 211 of the General Financial Rules (GFR), 2017 sets out the classification of stores and government assets for maintaining accounts and registers. Under Rule 211(1), every storekeeper or officer custodian is required to maintain distinct accounts and stock registers for: (i) Fixed Assets (such as plant, machinery, equipment, furniture, fixtures, land, and buildings in Form GFR-22); (ii) Consumables (items consumed, exhausted, or transformed during routine office operations like stationery, chemicals, fuel, and cleaning materials in Form GFR-23); and (iii) Non-consumables (durable items that do not qualify as permanent infrastructure but retain physical identity over time and are recorded in Form GFR-22/durable stores register). This tri-fold classification ensures accurate inventory valuation, proper physical verification, and systematic depreciation or write-off accounting in government establishments and schools.
explanation_hindi: सामान्य वित्तीय नियम (GFR), 2017 के नियम 211 के अनुसार, स्टॉक रजिस्टरों और लेखों के रखरखाव के लिए सरकारी संपत्तियों और भंडारों को स्पष्ट रूप से तीन प्रमुख श्रेणियों में वर्गीकृत किया गया है: (i) अचल परिसंपत्तियां (Fixed Assets) - जैसे संयंत्र, मशीनरी, उपकरण, फर्नीचर, भूमि व भवन, जिन्हें फॉर्म GFR-22 में दर्ज किया जाता है; (ii) उपभोज्य भंडार (Consumable Stores) - ऐसी वस्तुएं जो दैनिक कार्यालयीन या शैक्षणिक उपयोग में समाप्त/खर्च हो जाती हैं, जैसे स्टेशनरी, प्रयोगशाला रसायन, सफाई सामग्री आदि (फॉर्म GFR-23); और (iii) गैर-उपभोज्य भंडार (Non-consumable Stores) - टिकाऊ सामग्री जो लंबे समय तक उपयोग में रहती है और फॉर्म GFR-22 में दर्ज की जाती है। यह त्रि-स्तरीय वर्गीकरण सरकारी कार्यालयों और विद्यालयों में परिसंपत्तियों के समुचित सत्यापन, नियंत्रण और लेखांकन की नींव है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (B) Fixed assets, Consumable stores, and Non- consumable stores

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: consumable stores The General Financial Rules 2017 categorize government assets and stores into fixed assets, consumable stores, and non-consumable stores. Fixed assets include permanent infrastructure like land and buildings. Consumable stores encompass items used up during regular operations, while non-consumable stores consist of durable equipment, machinery, and office furniture requiring individual asset register maintenance. question_hindi:

I. अचल परिसंपत्तियों का रजिस्टर फॉर्म GFR-22 में बनाए रखा जाना चाहिए।

question_english:
Consider the following statements regarding the maintenance of an Asset Register under GFR 2017:
I. A Register of Fixed Assets must be maintained in the prescribed Form GFR-22.
II. Land, buildings, plant, and machinery are classified as fixed assets.
III. The asset register requires comprehensive details including cost, date of acquisition, and physical location.
IV. Fixed assets do not require any periodic physical verification.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
options_english: I, II and III only
I, III and IV only
II, III and IV only
I, II, III and IV
explanation_english:
Under GFR 2017:
- Statement I is correct: Rule 211(1)(i) explicitly mandates that the Register of Fixed Assets must be maintained in Form GFR-22.
- Statement II is correct: Fixed assets include permanent, immovable, and durable capital equipment such as land, buildings, plant, machinery, office vehicles, and standard apparatus.
- Statement III is correct: Form GFR-22 contains specific columns for entering the item description, serial number, historical purchase cost, date of acquisition, voucher reference, physical location/department, and disposal details.
- Statement IV is incorrect: Rule 213(1) of GFR 2017 explicitly states that physical verification of fixed assets must be conducted at least once in a year by a designated officer or committee to verify their physical existence, check working condition, and reconcile register balances with ground reality.
Therefore, statements I, II, and III are correct, making (A) the right option.
explanation_hindi:
सामान्य वित्तीय नियम (GFR), 2017 के तहत:
- कथन I सही है: नियम 211(1)(i) के अनुसार अचल परिसंपत्तियों का रजिस्टर फॉर्म GFR-22 में अनिवार्य रूप से रखा जाता है।
- कथन II सही है: भूमि, भवन, संयंत्र, मशीनरी, फर्नीचर और उपकरण अचल परिसंपत्तियों (Fixed Assets) के अंतर्गत आते हैं।
- कथन III सही है: फॉर्म GFR-22 में परिसंपत्ति का विवरण, अधिग्रहण की तिथि, खरीद मूल्य/लागत, वाउचर संख्या, आपूर्तिदाता का नाम और वर्तमान स्थान (लोकेशन) दर्ज करना अनिवार्य है।
- कथन IV गलत है: नियम 213(1) के अनुसार सभी अचल परिसंपत्तियों का वर्ष में कम से कम एक बार भौतिक सत्यापन (Physical Verification) अनिवार्य रूप से किया जाना चाहिए ताकि नुकसान, चोरी या अनुपयोगिता की पहचान हो सके।
अतः कथन I, II और III सही हैं, इसलिए विकल्प (A) सही उत्तर है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) I, II and III

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Fixed assets including land, buildings, plant, and machinery must be recorded in Form GFR-22, capturing acquisition costs, purchase dates, and physical locations. Contrary to ignoring physical checks, financial rules explicitly mandate periodic physical verification of all fixed assets to ensure structural existence, prevent unauthorized removal, and reconcile physical inventory with account registers.

question_hindi: किसी सरकारी विद्यालय का पुस्तकालयाध्यक्ष (लाइब्रेरियन) पुस्तकालय हेतु नई संदर्भ पुस्तकें खरीदता है। GFR के तहत, भंडार लेखांकन (Store Accounting) के प्रयोजन से इन पुस्तकों को किस प्रकार वर्गीकृत किया जाना चाहिए?

अत्यधिक तरल वित्तीय परिसंपत्तियां जिन्हें सीधे परिचालन नकदी में परिवर्तित किया जा सकता है।

question_english: The Librarian of a government school acquires new reference books and periodicals for the library. Under GFR 2017, how should these books be classified and treated for store accounting purposes?
options_english: As library books and publications, which are governed by dedicated accession register procedures.
As general consumable store items that are treated as completely exhausted within one year of procurement.
As standard heavy fixed assets alongside machinery, real estate, and permanent building structures.
As highly liquid financial assets readily convertible into direct operational cash.
explanation_english: Under Rule 215 of the General Financial Rules (GFR), 2017, library books and publications occupy a distinct category in government store accounting. They are neither treated as general consumable items (which are consumed/written off upon use) nor treated as standard dead-stock machinery/fixed assets. Instead, all purchased books and periodicals must be systematically recorded in an official Accession Register maintained by the library. GFR Rule 215 prescribes specialized procedures for the accessioning, custody, physical verification cycles (dependent on total holding volume), and write-off limits (allowing 5 volumes per 1,000 volumes issued/consulted in a year for ordinary wear and tear) for library collections.
explanation_hindi: सामान्य वित्तीय नियम (GFR), 2017 के नियम 215 के तहत, पुस्तकालय की पुस्तकों और पत्र-पत्रिकाओं को भंडार लेखांकन में एक विशिष्ट दर्जा प्राप्त है। इन्हें न तो सामान्य उपभोज्य भंडार (Consumable Store) माना जाता है और न ही सामान्य संयंत्र/मशीनरी जैसी अचल संपत्ति। पुस्तकालय की प्रत्येक पुस्तक को एक विशिष्ट 'परिग्रहण रजिस्टर' (Accession Register) में दर्ज किया जाता है। नियम 215 के अंतर्गत पुस्तकालय संग्रह के लिए पृथक भौतिक सत्यापन चक्र (पुस्तकों की कुल संख्या के आधार पर) तथा सामान्य टूट-फूट/नुकसान के अपलेखन (प्रति वर्ष निर्गत/संदर्भित 1,000 पुस्तकों पर 5 पुस्तकों तक का स्वीकार्य नुकसान) के विशेष नियम निर्धारित किए गए हैं।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) Library books and publications, which follow distinct accession register procedures.

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: distinct accession register procedures. Library books and publications are subject to distinct store accounting rules under financial regulations. Rather than being treated as immediate consumable items or standard machinery fixed assets, library collections are recorded in a dedicated Accession Register. Specific procedures govern their cataloging, physical verification frequencies, and write-off allowances for reasonable operational wear and tear.

question_hindi: GFR के तहत भंडारों के वर्गीकरण और प्रबंधन के संबंध में निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा कथन गलत (INCORRECT) है?

question_english: Identify the INCORRECT statement regarding the classification, maintenance, and handling of stores under GFR 2017.
options_english: Items such as office stationery, laboratory chemicals, and cleaning supplies are classified as consumable stores.
Computers, office furniture, and scientific apparatus are classified as non-consumable stores / fixed assets.
Non-consumable stores are written off and struck off from the asset register as soon as they are issued to an employee.
Consumable stores are those items that are utilized, transformed, or exhausted within a short timeframe through routine office use.
explanation_english: Under Rule 211 of GFR 2017, non-consumable stores encompass durable goods (e.g., computers, furniture, scientific instruments, sports gear). When such items are issued to a staff member, teacher, or department, it represents merely a transfer of operational/physical custody recorded through an internal issue register or custody receipt; it DOES NOT permit striking off or writing off the asset from the master Stock Register. A non-consumable item remains on the institution's books as a government asset throughout its useful life until it is surveyed by a condemnation board, declared surplus/unserviceable/obsolete under Rule 217-219, and formally written off by the competent financial authority. Hence, statement (C) is completely incorrect.
explanation_hindi: सामान्य वित्तीय नियम (GFR), 2017 के नियम 211 के अनुसार, गैर-उपभोज्य भंडार (Non-consumable stores) में टिकाऊ वस्तुएं जैसे कंप्यूटर, फर्नीचर, प्रयोगशाला उपकरण आदि शामिल होते हैं। जब ये वस्तुएं किसी कर्मचारी या विभाग को उपयोग हेतु जारी की जाती हैं, तो यह केवल भौतिक अभिरक्षा (Custody) का अंतरण होता है। इसे स्टॉक रजिस्टर से हटाया या बट्टे खाते (Write-off) में नहीं डाला जा सकता। यह वस्तु तब तक सरकारी संपत्ति रजिस्टर में बनी रहती है जब तक कि नियमानुसार (नियम 217-219 के तहत) एक सर्वेक्षण समिति द्वारा इसे अनुपयोगी, अप्रचलित या कबाड़ घोषित करके सक्षम प्राधिकारी द्वारा औपचारिक रूप से अपलेखित न कर दिया जाए। अतः कथन (C) गलत है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (C) Non-consumable stores are written off from the register as soon as issued to an employee.

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: the register as soon as issued to an employee. Non-consumable stores represent durable items like computers, furniture, and laboratory apparatus. Issuing non-consumable items to an employee or department transfers physical custody but does not permit writing them off from stock registers. They remain recorded assets until formally declared surplus, unserviceable, or condemned through established administrative procedures at the end of their useful life.

question_english:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).
Assertion (A): Fixed assets must be recorded in the government asset register at their original historical cost (purchase price).
Reason (R): GFR 2017 requires that the recorded value of fixed assets in the register be updated annually to reflect prevailing market inflation rates.
In light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options_english: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is true but (R) is false
(A) is false but (R) is true
explanation_english:
Under Form GFR-22 and Rule 211 of GFR 2017:
- Assertion (A) is true: Fixed assets and non-consumable stores must be recorded in Form GFR-22 at their original historical acquisition cost (which includes invoice price, statutory duties/taxes, freight, handling, and initial installation or commissioning charges).
- Reason (R) is false: Government accounting operates on the principle of historical cost accounting. GFR does not provide for or permit annual revaluation or upward indexation of asset register values based on fluctuating market inflation rates. The historical cost remains the benchmark until the asset is condemned and disposed of or depreciated where commercial/accrual accounting standards apply.
Therefore, (A) is true, but (R) is false.
explanation_hindi:
फॉर्म GFR-22 तथा GFR 2017 के नियम 211 के अनुसार:
- अभिकथन (A) सत्य है: सरकारी परिसंपत्ति रजिस्टर (फॉर्म GFR-22) में अचल परिसंपत्तियों को उनकी मूल ऐतिहासिक लागत (क्रय मूल्य, कर, भाड़ा तथा स्थापना लागत सहित) पर ही दर्ज किया जाता है।
- कारण (R) असत्य है: सरकारी लेखांकन प्रणाली में मुद्रास्फीति या बाजार दरों में उतार-चढ़ाव के आधार पर परिसंपत्ति रजिस्टर में दर्ज मूल्यों को प्रतिवर्ष संशोधित या पुनर्मूल्यांकित करने का कोई प्रावधान नहीं है। ऐतिहासिक लागत ही परिसंपत्ति के निपटान या अपलेखन तक प्रामाणिक अभिलेख मानी जाती है।
अतः (A) सही है लेकिन (R) गलत है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (C) (A) is true but (R) is false

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Fixed assets must be entered in asset registers at historical cost, representing their actual acquisition price including original installation expenses. Financial rules do not require annual reassessment or revaluation of register asset values based on fluctuating market inflation rates, ensuring consistent historical accounting records across official public property registers.

question_english:
Arrange the following administrative actions in the correct chronological sequence when a new non-consumable asset (e.g., a steel almirah) is procured by a government school:
I. Certification of receipt and satisfactory condition by the inspecting officer / committee.
II. Formal issue of the asset to the user department/teacher.
III. Recording the item along with its cost and invoice particulars in the Non-consumable Stock Register.
IV. Physical delivery of the consignment by the supplier.
Select the correct sequence using the options given below:
options_english: IV, I, III, II
I, IV, III, II
IV, III, I, II
I, II, III, IV
explanation_english:
Under Rule 208 and Rule 211 of GFR 2017, the standardized procedural sequence for receipt and issue of procured non-consumable stores is as follows:
1. Step IV: The contracted supplier delivers the goods/almirah to the school/office premises against a delivery challan.
2. Step I: The designated inspecting officer or purchase/inspection committee inspects the delivered item against technical specifications and certifies that it has been received in full quantity and good physical condition.
3. Step III: The storekeeper/custodian enters the item with its detailed description, serial number, supplier details, purchase order number, and cost into the Non-consumable Stock Register (Form GFR-22) and signs the stock certificate on the bill.
4. Step II: Once accessioned, the asset is formally issued to the concerned classroom, laboratory, or teacher against an issue voucher/internal custody register.
Thus, the correct chronological sequence is IV -> I -> III -> II.
explanation_hindi:
सामान्य वित्तीय नियम (GFR), 2017 के नियम 208 और नियम 211 के अनुसार नई गैर-उपभोज्य परिसंपत्ति की खरीद पर निम्नलिखित प्रक्रियागत अनुक्रम का पालन किया जाता है:
1. चरण IV: आपूर्तिकर्ता/विक्रेता द्वारा विद्यालय परिसर में सामान की भौतिक डिलीवरी (सुपुर्दगी) की जाती है।
2. चरण I: प्राधिकृत निरीक्षण अधिकारी या समिति सामग्री की गुणवत्ता व तकनीकी विशिष्टताओं का सत्यापन करती है तथा सामग्री के सही स्थिति में प्राप्त होने का प्रमाणन करती है।
3. चरण III: भंडार प्रभारी द्वारा गैर-उपभोज्य स्टॉक रजिस्टर (फॉर्म GFR-22) में सामग्री का विवरण, बिल संख्या, क्रय आदेश और लागत दर्ज की जाती है।
4. चरण II: स्टॉक प्रविष्टि के उपरांत ही सामग्री को संबंधित विभाग या शिक्षक को उपयोग हेतु जारी (Issue) किया जाता है।
अतः सही तार्किक क्रम IV -> I -> III -> II है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) IV, I, III, II

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: When acquiring new non-consumable assets, the supplier first delivers the items to the establishment. An inspecting officer verifies that the goods meet quality standards and issued purchase orders. Upon successful inspection, details and costs are recorded in the Non- consumable Stock Register before the asset is officially issued for departmental utilization.

question_english: Does GFR 2017 recognize "Intangible Assets" for the purpose of government asset accounting and store management, and if so, what represents a valid example?
options_english: No, GFR accounting principles deal strictly and exclusively with tangible physical stores and office furniture.
Yes, examples include enterprise software, digital databases, patents, and copyrights owned by the Government.
Yes, examples include commercial goodwill, public relations image, and the political reputation of the Ministry.
No, intangible financial assets are managed and accounted for exclusively by the Reserve Bank of India.
explanation_english: Under Rule 211 and Form GFR-22 / Form GFR-24 of the General Financial Rules (GFR), 2017, as well as Government Accounting Standards (IGAS), the government explicitly recognizes "Intangible Assets". Intangible assets are identifiable non-monetary assets without physical substance that are controlled by the government and hold enduring operational utility. Prime examples include customized computer software, enterprise application licenses, digital educational platforms, proprietary databases, patents, trade secrets, and intellectual copyrights acquired or developed using public funds. Establishments must record intangible assets in appropriate asset registers to maintain accountability over license renewals, intellectual property rights, and asset capitalization.
explanation_hindi: सामान्य वित्तीय नियम (GFR), 2017 के नियम 211 तथा सरकारी लेखा मानकों के अंतर्गत 'अमूर्त परिसंपत्तियों' (Intangible Assets) को परिसंपत्ति प्रबंधन और लेखांकन के प्रयोजनार्थ स्पष्ट रूप से मान्यता दी गई है। अमूर्त परिसंपत्तियां वे गैर-मौद्रिक परिसंपत्तियां हैं जिनका कोई भौतिक स्वरूप नहीं होता, लेकिन वे संस्था के लिए दीर्घकालिक मूल्य रखती हैं। सरकारी कार्यालयों और विद्यालयों में इसके प्रमुख उदाहरणों में सरकार के स्वामित्व वाले विशिष्ट सॉफ्टवेयर लाइसेंस, डिजिटल डेटाबेस, पेटेंट, बौद्धिक संपदा अधिकार और कॉपीराइट शामिल हैं। इन्हें सरकारी परिसंपत्ति रजिस्टर में दर्ज कर उनकी वैधता और उपयोग का उचित रिकॉर्ड रखना अनिवार्य होता है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (B) Yes, examples include software, patents, and copyrights owned by Government.

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: copyrights owned by Government. General Financial Rules recognize intangible assets for property accounting and management purposes. Intangible assets represent non- physical valuable rights, including specialized software licenses, patents, intellectual property rights, and copyrights owned by government organizations. Establishments must maintain appropriate accounting records to track acquisitions, usage rights, and financial values of intangible assets.

question_english: Which of the following pairs concerning the statutory forms prescribed under GFR 2017 for maintenance of store accounts is correctly matched?
options_english: Form GFR 22 - Register of Consumables
Form GFR 23 - Register of Fixed Assets
Form GFR 21 - Accession Register for Library Books
Form GFR 22 - Register of Fixed Assets
explanation_english:
Under Rule 211 of GFR 2017:
- Form GFR-22 is the prescribed statutory format for the 'Register of Fixed Assets' (Rule 211(1)(i)), which captures durable assets like plant, machinery, furniture, equipment, and motor vehicles.
- Form GFR-23 is the prescribed format for the 'Register of Consumables' (Rule 211(1)(ii)), used for expendable supplies such as stationery, laboratory chemicals, and cleaning materials.
- Form GFR-24 is prescribed for the 'Register of Assets of Historical / Artistic Value'.
Therefore, the pairing in option (D) 'Form GFR 22 - Register of Fixed Assets' is perfectly matched.
explanation_hindi:
सामान्य वित्तीय नियम (GFR), 2017 के नियम 211 के तहत निर्धारित प्रपत्र इस प्रकार हैं:
- फॉर्म GFR-22: 'अचल परिसंपत्तियों का रजिस्टर' (Register of Fixed Assets) - नियम 211(1)(i) के तहत संयंत्र, मशीनरी, उपकरण, फर्नीचर आदि के लिए निर्धारित है।
- फॉर्म GFR-23: 'उपभोज्य भंडार का रजिस्टर' (Register of Consumables) - नियम 211(1)(ii) के तहत स्टेशनरी, रसायन व उपभोज्य वस्तुओं के लिए निर्धारित है।
- फॉर्म GFR-24: ऐतिहासिक या कलात्मक महत्व की परिसंपत्तियों का रजिस्टर है।
अतः विकल्प (D) 'फॉर्म GFR 22 - अचल परिसंपत्तियों का रजिस्टर' सही सुमेलित है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (D) Form GFR 22 - Register of Fixed Assets

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Under the General Financial Rules 2017, Form GFR-22 is the standard prescribed format for maintaining the Register of Fixed Assets. Public establishments must utilize Form GFR-22 to record essential details of fixed assets, including description, acquisition date, cost, location, and details regarding physical verification or ultimate asset disposal.

question_english: According to Rule 213 of GFR 2017, how frequently must the physical verification of fixed assets in a government office or school be carried out?
options_english: At least once in a year
At least once every month
At least once in three years

explanation_english: Under Rule 213(1) of the General Financial Rules (GFR), 2017, the physical verification of fixed assets (recorded in Form GFR-22) must be conducted at least once in a year. The verification officer or committee must physically inspect each asset to confirm its existence, condition, and location, and subsequently record the verification certificate and remarks in the Register of Fixed Assets. Any discrepancy, shortage, or unserviceable condition identified during the annual verification must be promptly reported to the Head of Office / competent authority for investigation and administrative remedial action.
explanation_hindi: सामान्य वित्तीय नियम (GFR), 2017 के नियम 213(1) के अनुसार, सरकारी कार्यालय अथवा विद्यालय में सभी अचल परिसंपत्तियों (फॉर्म GFR-22 में दर्ज) का भौतिक सत्यापन (Physical Verification) वर्ष में कम से कम एक बार (at least once in a year) अनिवार्य रूप से किया जाना चाहिए। सत्यापन अधिकारी अथवा समिति द्वारा परिसंपत्तियों की भौतिक उपस्थिति, कार्यदशा और स्थिति की जांच कर उसका प्रमाणपत्र रजिस्टर में दर्ज किया जाता है। यदि सत्यापन के दौरान कोई कमी, क्षति या अंतर पाया जाता है, तो उसे तत्काल सक्षम प्राधिकारी के संज्ञान में लाया जाना चाहिए।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) At least once a year

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Rule 213 of the General Financial Rules 2017 mandates that physical verification of fixed assets must be conducted at least once every year. The physical verification process verifies the physical existence and condition of assets, helps reconcile physical records with stock registers, and identifies missing, damaged, or unserviceable items requiring administrative action.

question_english:
Consider the following statements regarding the physical verification of stores under GFR 2017:
I. The verification must be carried out in the presence of the officer or custodian responsible for the physical custody of the stores.
II. Discrepancies, shortages, or damages detected during verification must be brought to the notice of the competent authority immediately.
III. The verification should ideally be conducted by the storekeeper who maintains the stock registers.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
options_english: I and II only
II and III only
I and III only
I, II and III
explanation_english:
Under Rule 213 of GFR 2017:
- Statement I is correct: Physical verification must be conducted in the presence of the officer responsible for the custody of the stores or their authorized nominee, so that any physical movement or query can be clarified on the spot.
- Statement II is correct: Rule 213(3) explicitly mandates that shortages, damages, unserviceable items, or surplus inventory revealed during physical verification must be promptly brought to the notice of the competent authority for investigation and necessary adjustment.
- Statement III is incorrect: Rule 213(2) strictly dictates that the verification must NEVER be conducted by a person who is the storekeeper, who has physical custody of the stores, or who is directly subordinate to the storekeeper. An independent officer or committee must be entrusted with verification to prevent bias, concealment, and conflict of interest.
Hence, statements I and II are correct, making (A) the correct choice.
explanation_hindi:
सामान्य वित्तीय नियम (GFR), 2017 के नियम 213 के अनुसार:
- कथन I सही है: भंडारों का भौतिक सत्यापन सदैव उस अधिकारी या कर्मचारी की उपस्थिति में किया जाना चाहिए जो उन भंडारों की वास्तविक अभिरक्षा (Custody) के लिए जिम्मेदार है।
- कथन II सही है: नियम 213(3) के अनुसार सत्यापन के दौरान यदि कोई कमी (Shortage), क्षति (Damage) या अन्य विसंगतियां पाई जाती हैं, तो उन्हें बिना किसी विलंब के सक्षम प्राधिकारी के संज्ञान में लाया जाना अनिवार्य है ताकि जवाबदेही तय की जा सके।
- कथन III गलत है: नियम 213(2) में स्पष्ट प्रावधान है कि भौतिक सत्यापन कभी भी उस स्टोर-कीपर या उसके सीधे अधीनस्थ कर्मचारी द्वारा नहीं किया जाएगा जिसके पास भंडारों की अभिरक्षा या रिकॉर्ड रखने का प्रभार है। निष्पक्षता सुनिश्चित करने के लिए यह कार्य किसी स्वतंत्र अधिकारी या समिति द्वारा ही किया जाना चाहिए।
अतः केवल कथन I और II सही हैं।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) I and II

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Physical verification of stores must be conducted in the presence of the store custodian, and any detected shortages, damages, or discrepancies must be immediately reported to competent authorities. To ensure objective verification, the inspection must be conducted by an independent officer or committee, never by the storekeeper responsible for stock custody.

question_english: The Principal of a government school intends to constitute an annual physical verification committee for the school's sports equipment and gym stores. To strictly comply with GFR 2017, whom should the Principal appoint to conduct this verification?
options_english: An independent officer or committee excluding the custodian of the sports store.
The Physical Education Teacher (PET) who holds official charge and custody of the sports store.
The commercial sports vendor who originally supplied the equipment to the school.
A committee composed exclusively of Group D support staff members of the institution.
explanation_english: Under Rule 213(2) of GFR 2017, physical verification of stores must be carried out by an independent officer or committee who is neither the custodian of the stores nor subordinate to the custodian. In a school setting, the Physical Education Teacher (PET) or sports in-charge is the custodian who indents, receives, maintains, and issues sports goods. Allowing the PET to verify their own store would create a direct conflict of interest and defeat the fundamental internal check required by public financial rules. External vendors have no official standing in internal government verification, and Group D employees cannot take administrative responsibility. Therefore, the Principal must appoint an independent committee of other teaching/administrative officers (e.g., Vice-Principal, PGTs) in whose presence the PET will present the inventory for physical counting.
explanation_hindi: सामान्य वित्तीय नियम (GFR), 2017 के नियम 213(2) के अनुसार, भंडारों का भौतिक सत्यापन किसी ऐसे स्वतंत्र अधिकारी या समिति द्वारा किया जाना चाहिए जिसके पास उन भंडारों की अभिरक्षा (Custody) न हो। विद्यालय में शारीरिक शिक्षा शिक्षक (PET) खेल सामग्री के आधिकारिक अभिरक्षक होते हैं। यदि PET को ही अपने भंडार के सत्यापन का जिम्मा दिया जाए, तो यह 'हितों के टकराव' (Conflict of Interest) का स्पष्ट मामला होगा और वित्तीय नियंत्रण का उद्देश्य विफल हो जाएगा। बाहरी विक्रेता का सरकारी सत्यापन से कोई संबंध नहीं है और न ही केवल ग्रुप 'डी' कर्मचारियों को यह प्रशासनिक जिम्मेदारी दी जा सकती है। अतः प्रधानाचार्य को खेल भंडार के अभिरक्षक से भिन्न स्वतंत्र शिक्षकों/अधिकारियों की एक समिति गठित करनी चाहिए।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) An officer other than the custodian of the sports store, ideally a committee.

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: sports store, ideally a committee. To ensure objectivity and prevent potential conflict of interest, financial rules require that physical verification of stores be conducted by an officer or committee independent of store custody. Appointing the store custodian or physical education teacher in charge of the Click Here to Buy book on Flipkart sports store to verify their own stock is strictly prohibited under verification rules.

question_english:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).
Assertion (A): Complete physical verification of library books in large public/educational institutions is conducted periodically in cycles rather than annually if the library possesses a large volume of books (e.g., exceeding 50,000 volumes).
Reason (R): GFR 2017 prescribes tiered verification frequencies linked to the total holding size of the library to ensure operational feasibility without disrupting day-to-day library operations.
In light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options_english: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is true but (R) is false
(A) is false but (R) is true
explanation_english:
Under Rule 215 of the General Financial Rules (GFR), 2017, physical verification of library books is governed by volume-based statutory schedules:
1. Libraries with not more than 20,000 volumes: complete physical verification must be undertaken at least once a year.
2. Libraries with more than 20,000 and up to 50,000 volumes: physical verification should be done at least once in three years.
3. Libraries having more than 50,000 volumes: physical verification should be carried out at least once in three years, or sample verification of not less than 10% of volumes may be conducted annually so that the entire library is covered within five years.
Thus, Assertion (A) is completely true, Reason (R) accurately captures the rationale behind tiered frequencies under GFR Rule 215, and Reason (R) is the direct and correct explanation of Assertion (A).
explanation_hindi:

3. 50,000 से अधिक पुस्तकों वाले बड़े पुस्तकालय: तीन वर्ष में कम से कम एक बार, अथवा प्रतिवर्ष कम से कम 10% पुस्तकों का नमूना (सैंपल) सत्यापन जिससे 5 वर्षों में संपूर्ण पुस्तकालय कवर हो जाए।
अतः बड़े पुस्तकालयों में दैनिक पठन-पाठन और परिचालन बाधित न हो, इसके लिए वार्षिक के बजाय आवधिक/चक्रीय सत्यापन का नियम बनाया गया है। इसलिए (A) और (R) दोनों सही हैं तथा (R), (A) की सही व्याख्या है।

Consequently, financial rules prescribe sample physical checks or staggered multi-year verification cycles based on total holdings, establishing practical sample sizes and intervals to ensure inventory oversight without disrupting library services.

question_hindi: GFR के अनुसार पुस्तकालय की पुस्तकों के भौतिक सत्यापन और अपलेखन के संबंध में निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा कथन गलत (INCORRECT) है?

यदि कोई पुस्तक खो जाती है, तो बिना किसी जांच के उसकी कीमत तुरंत पुस्तकालयाध्यक्ष (लाइब्रेरियन) के वेतन से वसूल की जानी चाहिए।

question_english: Which of the following statements is INCORRECT regarding the physical verification and write-off of library books under GFR 2017?
options_english: For libraries with not more than 20,000 volumes, complete physical verification must be conducted at least once a year.
Any loss of a book must be automatically recovered from the Librarian's monthly salary without conducting an inquiry.
For libraries having more than 20,000 but up to 50,000 volumes, verification should be done at least once in three years.
Loss of up to 5 volumes per 1,000 volumes of books issued or consulted in a year may be taken as reasonable wear and tear and written off.
explanation_english: Under Rule 215 of GFR 2017, the rules acknowledge that in libraries with open access and frequent circulation, a minor loss of books is an inevitable operational reality. Rule 215(3) specifically provides: "Loss of five volumes per one thousand volumes of books issued/consulted in a year may be taken as reasonable loss, but the loss of a book of a value exceeding the monetary limit... shall be reported to the competent authority for inquiry." Automatically deducting the cost of lost books from the Librarian's salary without holding a fact-finding inquiry or establishing willful dishonesty, gross negligence, or lack of reasonable care is illegal, arbitrary, and strictly contrary to GFR provisions and principles of natural justice. Hence, option (B) is the incorrect statement.
explanation_hindi: सामान्य वित्तीय नियम (GFR), 2017 के नियम 215(3) के अनुसार, पुस्तकालयों में नियमित उपयोग और ओपन एक्सेस के कारण कुछ पुस्तकों का खो जाना स्वाभाविक माना जाता है। नियम के अनुसार, एक वर्ष में जारी अथवा परामर्शित (Issued/Consulted) प्रति 1,000 पुस्तकों पर 5 पुस्तकों तक के नुकसान को सामान्य टूट-फूट (Reasonable loss) मानकर सक्षम प्राधिकारी द्वारा बट्टे खाते में डाला (Write-off) जा सकता है। बिना किसी विभागीय जांच या जानबूझकर की गई लापरवाही/गबन सिद्ध हुए बिना, सीधे पुस्तकालयाध्यक्ष के वेतन से वसूली करना नियमों के सर्वथा विरुद्ध और मनमाना है। अतः कथन (B) गलत है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (B) Any loss of a book must be recovered from the Librarian's salary without inquiry.

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: the Librarian's salary without inquiry. Financial rules recognize that minor book losses in public libraries occur naturally through routine consultation and circulation. Rules permit writing off up to five volumes per thousand issued or consulted books annually as normal wear and tear. Automatically recovering book values from a librarian's salary without conducting an inquiry is arbitrary and prohibited.

question_english: How frequently does Rule 213 of GFR 2017 mandate the physical verification of consumable goods and materials (such as office stationery and laboratory chemicals)?
options_english: Twice a year
Every month

Once in five years
explanation_english: Under Rule 213(2) of the General Financial Rules (GFR), 2017, "Physical verification of Consumables: A physical verification of all the consumable goods and materials should be undertaken at least once in a year and subject to verification of the records." This annual verification enables the Head of Office and inspecting authorities to reconcile physical stock balances in stores with entries in the Consumables Register (Form GFR-23), verify consumption patterns, and detect any leakage, pilferage, or abnormal spoilage in a timely manner.
explanation_hindi: सामान्य वित्तीय नियम (GFR), 2017 के नियम 213(2) के अनुसार, 'उपभोज्य वस्तुओं का भौतिक सत्यापन' (Physical verification of Consumables) वर्ष में कम से कम एक बार (at least once in a year) अनिवार्य रूप से किया जाना चाहिए। यह वार्षिक सत्यापन कार्यालय प्रमुख और लेखा अधिकारियों को उपभोज्य रजिस्टर (फॉर्म GFR-23) के अभिलेखों के साथ वास्तविक भौतिक स्टॉक का मिलान करने, उपभोग के पैटर्न की निगरानी करने तथा सामग्री की किसी भी प्रकार की बर्बादी, लीकेज या चोरी को समय पर पकड़ने में सक्षम बनाता है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (C) Once a year

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Rule 213 of the General Financial Rules 2017 requires that physical verification of consumable stores, such as office stationery, laboratory chemicals, and cleaning supplies, be carried out at least once every year. This annual verification reconciles physical stock with consumption registers and ensures timely detection of waste, leakage, or stock discrepancies.

question_hindi: आईटी प्रयोगशाला (IT Lab) के भौतिक सत्यापन (Physical Verification) के दौरान सत्यापन समिति को पता चलता है कि दो डेस्कटॉप मॉनिटर गायब हैं। जीएफआर (GFR), 2017 के नियमों के अनुसार इस निष्कर्ष का तात्कालिक परिणाम क्या होगा?
options_hindi: गायब मॉनिटरों को बिना किसी औपचारिक प्रशासनिक प्रक्रिया के स्टॉक रजिस्टर से स्वतः ही हटा दिया जाता है।
भौतिक सत्यापन समिति के सदस्यों को गायब मॉनिटरों की क्रय लागत का व्यक्तिगत रूप से भुगतान करना होगा।
कमी को छिपाने के लिए विद्यालय प्रशासन को स्थानीय/छात्र निधि से चुपचाप प्रतिस्थापन मॉनिटर खरीदने होंगे।
विसंगति (Discrepancy) को तुरंत अभिलिखित किया जाना चाहिए और कार्यालयाध्यक्ष (Head of Office) को जिम्मेदारी तय करने के लिए जांच शुरू करनी चाहिए।
